title.zh: 卷九十四 列傳第五十四 恩倖
title.raw: 卷九十四 列傳第五十四 恩倖 Volume 94 Biographies 54: En Xing

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十四 恩幸

translations.literal: Biography 54: Favored Favorites
translations.idiomatic: Biography 54: Those Favored by Imperial Grace

sentences.zh: 夫君子小人，類物之稱。

translations.literal: As for the gentleman and the petty man, they are terms for kinds of persons.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman and the petty man are merely names for two kinds of human beings.

sentences.zh: 蹈道則為君子，違之則為小人。

translations.literal: Treading the Way makes one a gentleman; violating it makes one a petty man.
translations.idiomatic: Follow the Way and you are counted a gentleman; depart from it and you are a petty man.

sentences.zh: 屠釣，卑事也；

translations.literal: Butchering and fishing are lowly occupations;
translations.idiomatic: Butchering and angling were humble trades;

sentences.zh: 版築，賤役也，太公起為周師，傅說去為殷相。

translations.literal: Rammed-earth labor was a menial service; yet the Grand Duke rose to be Zhou's preceptor, and Fuyue left it to become Yin's chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Rammed-earth labor was work for commoners, yet Taigong rose to become preceptor to Zhou, and Fuyue left the worksites to serve as minister to the Yin.

sentences.zh: 非論公侯之世，鼎食之資，明揚幽仄，唯才是與。

translations.literal: It was not a matter of discussing the age of marquises and earls or inheritance of grand stipends; the enlightened elevated the obscure and lowly, conferring posts solely on talent.
translations.idiomatic: This was not limited to an age when only lords and great houses held ritual-tripod stipends; the enlightened sought out hidden worth and granted office purely according to ability.

sentences.zh: 逮於二漢，茲道未革，胡廣累世農夫，伯始致位公相；

translations.literal: Down through the two Han dynasties this principle was not abolished: Hu Guang's family were farmers for generations, yet Boya reached the rank of chief minister;
translations.idiomatic: By the two Han dynasties this practice had not been abandoned: Hu Guang came from generations of farming folk, yet as Bo Shi he rose to the highest offices of state;

sentences.zh: 黃憲牛醫之子，叔度名重京師。

translations.literal: Huang Xian was the son of an ox doctor, yet Shudu was renowned throughout the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Xian was the son of a cattle doctor, yet Shudu made a name for himself throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 且任子居朝，鹹有職業，雖七葉珥貂，見崇西漢，而侍中身奉奏事，又分掌禦服。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the Ren clan served at court, each had his proper occupation; though for seven generations they wore the courtier's sable ear-pendants and were honored in Western Han, the Palace Attendant personally presented memorials and also shared charge of the imperial wardrobe.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when members of the Ren family held office at court, each had a proper profession; though for seven generations they wore the courtier's sable pendants and were honored in Western Han, the Palace Attendant still personally presented memorials and also shared supervision of the imperial wardrobe.

sentences.zh: 東方朔為黃門侍郎，執戟殿下。

translations.literal: Dongfang Shuo served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, halberd in hand below the palace steps.
translations.idiomatic: Dongfang Shuo served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, standing halberd in hand beneath the palace steps.

sentences.zh: 郡縣掾史，並出豪家，負戈宿衛，皆由勢族，非若晚代，分為二途者也。

translations.literal: County and district clerks and recorders all came from powerful families; those who bore arms on night guard duty likewise arose from influential clans—not as in later ages, when the paths were divided in two.
translations.idiomatic: County and district clerks all came from powerful families, and men who bore arms on night guard likewise arose from influential clans—nothing like later times, when the two paths were rigidly separated.

sentences.zh: 漢末喪亂，魏武始基，軍中倉卒，權立九品。

translations.literal: At the end of Han came turmoil and ruin; when Emperor Wu of Wei laid his foundations, amid the haste of the army he provisionally established the nine ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Han came chaos and ruin; when Cao Cao laid his foundations, amid the urgency of military affairs he provisionally established the nine-rank system.

sentences.zh: 蓋以論人才優劣，非為世族高卑。

translations.literal: It was meant to assess the superiority or inferiority of talent, not the high or low standing of hereditary clans.
translations.idiomatic: It was meant to judge the quality of talent, not the standing of hereditary clans.

sentences.zh: 因此相沿，遂為成法。

translations.literal: From this it was handed down and became established law.
translations.idiomatic: Passed down in this way, it became fixed law.

sentences.zh: 自魏至晉，莫之能改，州都郡正，以才品人，而舉世人才，升降蓋寡。

translations.literal: From Wei through Jin none could alter it; provincial and commandery Rectifiers graded men by talent, yet throughout the realm the rise and fall of persons of ability was exceedingly slight.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei through Jin no one could change it; provincial and commandery Rectifiers graded men by talent, yet throughout the realm there was scarcely any real rise or fall among men of ability.

sentences.zh: 徒以馮藉世資，用相陵駕，都正俗士，斟酌時宜，品目少多，隨事俯仰，劉毅所雲「下品無高門，上品無賤族」者也。

translations.literal: Men relied solely on hereditary standing to overbear one another; the Rectifiers, being vulgar fellows, adjusted to the times, assigning more or fewer grades as circumstances required, bowing and yielding as the occasion demanded—precisely what Liu Yi meant when he said, "In the lower ranks there are no great houses; in the upper ranks there are no base clans."
translations.idiomatic: Men relied solely on hereditary standing to dominate one another; the Rectifiers, being men of no distinction, adjusted to the times, assigning grades high or low as circumstances required, bending with every shift in fortune—precisely what Liu Yi meant when he said, "The lower ranks have no great houses; the upper ranks have no base clans."

sentences.zh: 歲月遷訛，斯風漸篤，凡厥衣冠，莫非二品，自此以還，遂成卑庶。

translations.literal: As years passed and customs shifted, this tendency grew ever firmer: all who wore caps and robes were none but of the second rank; from that rank downward, one became base commoners.
translations.idiomatic: As years passed, this tendency grew ever stronger: everyone who wore cap and robe was counted at least second rank; from that level downward, one was classed as base commoner.

sentences.zh: 周、漢之道，以智役愚，台隸參差，用成等級；

translations.literal: The way of Zhou and Han was for the wise to employ the foolish; clerks and attendants were graded in rank, thereby forming a hierarchy;
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhou and Han way, the wise employed the foolish; clerks and attendants were graded in rank, thereby forming a hierarchy;

sentences.zh: 魏晉以來，以貴役賤，士庶之科，較然有辨。

translations.literal: Since Wei and Jin, the noble have employed the base; the categories of gentry and commoner have been clearly distinct.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei and Jin, the noble have employed the base; the lines between gentry and commoner have been sharply drawn.

sentences.zh: 夫人君南面，九重奧絕，陪奉朝夕，義隔卿士，階闥之任，宜有司存。

translations.literal: When the ruler faces south, the ninefold inner palace is remote and sealed; those who attend him morning and evening are separated in duty from ministers and grandees; tasks at the steps and gates ought to be assigned to proper offices.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler faces south, the inner palace's ninefold gates stand remote and sealed; those who attend him day and night are set apart in duty from ministers and grandees; duties at the steps and gates ought to belong to proper offices.

sentences.zh: 既而恩以幸生，信由恩固，無可憚之姿，有易親之色。

translations.literal: Then favor gave birth to intimacy, and trust was secured through favor; they had no aspect that inspired awe, but a manner easy to draw near.
translations.idiomatic: Then favor bred intimacy, and trust was secured through favor; they had nothing about them that inspired awe, but a manner easy to approach.

sentences.zh: 孝建、泰始，主威獨運，官置百司，權不外假，而刑政糾雜，理難遍通，耳目所寄，事歸近習。

translations.literal: In the Xiaojian and Taishi eras the sovereign's authority operated alone; though the hundred offices were established and power was not lent abroad, penal administration and government were tangled and complex, reason could not reach everywhere, and what the eyes and ears relied upon fell to those in close attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaojian and Taishi eras the sovereign wielded authority alone; though the hundred offices were in place and power was not delegated outward, penal administration and government were tangled and complex, and reason could not reach everywhere—so what the ruler's eyes and ears depended on fell to those in close attendance.

sentences.zh: 賞罰之要，是謂國權，出內王命，由其掌握，於是方途結軌，輻湊同奔。

translations.literal: The essentials of reward and punishment are what is called state authority; issuing and withdrawing the royal command lay in their grasp, and so from every direction wheels joined on the track and spokes converged in a single rush.
translations.idiomatic: The essentials of reward and punishment are the core of state authority; issuing and withdrawing the royal command lay in their hands, and so from every direction men converged like wheel spokes on a hub.

sentences.zh: 人主謂其身卑位薄，以為權不得重。

translations.literal: The ruler supposed that because their persons were lowly and their posts slight, their power could not be weighty.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler supposed that because their persons were lowly and their posts slight, their power could not amount to much.

sentences.zh: 曾不知鼠憑社貴，狐藉虎威，外無逼主之嫌，內有專用之功，勢傾天下，未之或悟。

translations.literal: He did not realize that the rat is honored through its earth-god mound, the fox borrows the tiger's might—outwardly there was no suspicion of pressing upon the ruler, inwardly they had the merit of exclusive use; their power tilted the realm, yet none perceived it.
translations.idiomatic: He failed to see that the rat is honored through its shrine-mound, the fox borrows the tiger's might—outwardly there was no appearance of coercing the ruler, inwardly they held exclusive control; their power tilted the realm, yet none perceived it.

sentences.zh: 挾朋樹黨，政以賄成，鈇鉞創磐，構於筵笫之曲，服冕乘軒，出乎言笑之下。

translations.literal: Clutching factions and planting parties, government was accomplished through bribes; axes and halberds were forged amid the curves of banquet mats; wearing coronets and riding high carriages arose from beneath a jest or smile.
translations.idiomatic: Clutching factions and planting parties, they made government through bribes; axes and halberds were forged amid the curves of banquet mats; coronets and high carriages were granted from beneath a jest or smile.

sentences.zh: 南金北毳，來悉方艚，素縑丹魄，至皆兼兩，西京許、史，蓋不足雲，晉朝王、庾，未或能比。

translations.literal: Southern gold and northern furs arrived in whole square-prowed ships; plain silk and cinnabar ore came in loads of two piculs each—the Xus and Shis of Western Capital scarcely bear mention; Wang and Yu of Jin could not compare.
translations.idiomatic: Southern gold and northern furs arrived in whole cargo ships; plain silk and cinnabar ore came in double-picul loads—the Xus and Shis of Western Capital scarcely bear mention; the Wang and Yu of Jin could not compare.

sentences.zh: 及太宗晚運，慮經盛衰，權幸之徒，懾憚宗戚，欲使幼主孤立，永竊國權，構造同異，興樹禍隙，帝弟宗王，相繼屠劋。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming's late reign came, mindful that prosperity and decline had been witnessed, the power-favored feared the imperial clan; wishing to leave the young ruler isolated and usurp state authority forever, they fabricated differences and raised rifts of disaster; the emperor's younger brothers and imperial princes were slaughtered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Ming's late reign, mindful that he had seen both rise and fall, the power-favored feared the imperial clan; wishing to isolate the young ruler and seize state authority forever, they manufactured divisions and sowed disasters; the emperor's younger brothers and imperial princes were cut down one after another.

sentences.zh: 民忘宋德，雖非一途，寶祚夙傾，實由於此。

translations.literal: The people forgot Song's virtue—though the causes were not one alone—the imperial mandate had long since tilted, and this was truly the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The people forgot the virtue of Song—though the causes were not one alone—the throne had long been tilting, and this was truly the reason.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 《漢書》有《恩澤侯表》，又有《佞幸傳》。

translations.literal: The Book of Han has the "Table of Marquises Favored by Grace" and also the "Biographies of Sycophants."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Han has the "Table of Marquises Favored by Grace" and also the "Biographies of Fawning Favorites."

sentences.zh: 今采其名，列以為《恩幸篇》雲。

translations.literal: Now taking their names, I arrange them as the "Treatise on Favored Favorites," thus.
translations.idiomatic: Now taking their names, I arrange them in this "Treatise on Those Favored by Imperial Grace."

sentences.zh: 戴法興，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Dai Faxing was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 家貧，父碩子，販珝為業。

translations.literal: His family was poor; his father Shuozi made a living selling ramie cloth.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor; his father Shuozi made a living selling ramie cloth.

sentences.zh: 法興二兄延壽、延興並修立，延壽善書，法興好學。

translations.literal: Faxing's two elder brothers Yanshou and Yanxing were both upright and accomplished; Yanshou excelled at calligraphy, Faxing loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing's two elder brothers Yanshou and Yanxing were both upright and accomplished; Yanshou excelled at calligraphy, while Faxing loved learning.

sentences.zh: 山陰有陳載者，家富，有錢三千萬，鄉人咸云：「戴碩子三兒，敵陳載三千萬錢。」

translations.literal: In Shanyin there was a Chen Zai, whose family was wealthy and possessed thirty million in cash; the villagers all said, "Shuozi's three sons of the Dai family are a match for Chen Zai's thirty million."
translations.idiomatic: In Shanyin there was a Chen Zai whose family was wealthy and held thirty million in cash; the villagers all said, "Shuozi's three sons of the Dai family are worth as much as Chen Zai's thirty million."

sentences.zh: 世祖親覽朝政，不任大臣，而腹心耳目，不得無所委寄。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu personally reviewed court affairs and did not entrust great ministers, yet his intimate confidants and eyes and ears could not be left without someone to rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu personally oversaw court affairs and did not rely on great ministers, yet his intimate confidants and eyes and ears had to be entrusted to someone.

sentences.zh: 法興頗知古今，素見親待，雖出侍東宮，而意任隆密。

translations.literal: Faxing was fairly versed in past and present and had long been treated with intimacy; though he went out to attend the Eastern Palace, the emperor's trust in him remained weighty and close.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing was fairly versed in past and present and had long been treated with intimacy; though he went out to attend the Eastern Palace, the emperor's trust in him remained profound and close.

sentences.zh: 魯郡巢尚之，人士之末，元嘉中，侍始興王浚讀書，亦涉獵文史，為上所知。

translations.literal: Chao Shangzhi of Lu commandery stood at the lower edge of cultivated men; in the Yuanjia era he attended Prince Shixing Liu Jun in his studies, also ranged through literature and history, and came to the emperor's notice.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Shangzhi of Lu commandery stood at the lower edge of cultivated society; in the Yuanjia era he attended Prince Shixing Liu Jun in his studies, also ranged through literature and history, and came to the emperor's notice.

sentences.zh: 孝建初，補東海國侍郎，仍兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian he was appointed Attendant of Donghai kingdom, and concurrently served as Palace Secretariat Communications Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xiaojian era he was appointed Attendant of the Donghai kingdom and concurrently served as Palace Secretariat Communications Attendant.

sentences.zh: 凡選授遷轉誅賞大處分，上皆與法興、尚之參懷，內外諸雜事，多委明寶。

translations.literal: For all major decisions of selection, appointment, transfer, punishment, reward, and the like, the emperor consulted with Faxing and Shangzhi; most other internal and external miscellaneous affairs were entrusted to Mingbao.
translations.idiomatic: For all major decisions of selection, appointment, transfer, punishment, and reward, the emperor consulted with Faxing and Shangzhi; most other internal and external miscellaneous affairs were entrusted to Mingbao.

sentences.zh: 上性嚴暴，睚眥之間，動至罪戮，尚之每臨事解釋，多得全免，殿省甚賴之。

translations.literal: The emperor's nature was severe and violent; over the slightest grudge he would move to punishment and execution; Shangzhi whenever he faced such matters would explain and intercede, and many were wholly spared—the palace offices relied on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's nature was severe and violent; over the slightest grudge he would move to punishment and execution; Shangzhi would explain and intercede whenever such matters arose, and many were wholly spared—the palace offices relied on him greatly.

sentences.zh: 而法興、明寶大通人事，多納貨賄，凡所薦達，言無不行，天下輻湊，門外成市，家產並累千金。

translations.literal: Yet Faxing and Mingbao were thoroughly versed in human affairs and accepted many bribes; whatever they recommended was never refused; the realm converged upon them, a market formed outside their gates, and each household's wealth mounted to a thousand in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Faxing and Mingbao were thoroughly versed in human affairs and accepted many bribes; whatever they recommended was never refused; the realm converged upon them until a market formed outside their gates, and each household's wealth mounted to a thousand in gold.

sentences.zh: 明寶驕縱尤甚，長子敬為揚州從事，與上爭買禦物。

translations.literal: Mingbao's arrogance and license were especially extreme; his eldest son Jing served as Yangzhou Registrar and vied with the emperor in buying imperial goods.
translations.idiomatic: Mingbao's arrogance and license were especially extreme; his eldest son Jing served as Yangzhou Registrar and vied with the emperor in buying imperial goods.

sentences.zh: 六宮嘗出行，敬盛服騎馬于車左右，馳驟去來。

translations.literal: When the inner palace once went out on procession, Jing in full dress rode a horse to the left and right of the carriage, galloping back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: When the inner palace once went out on procession, Jing in full dress rode a horse to the left and right of the carriage, galloping back and forth.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，賜敬死，系明寶尚方，尋被原釋，委任如初。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged, granted Jing death, and imprisoned Mingbao in the Imperial Workshop; soon he was pardoned and released, and his commission was as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly enraged, ordered Jing to die, and imprisoned Mingbao in the Imperial Workshop; soon he was pardoned and released, and his commission was as before.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，前廢帝即位，法興遷越騎校尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu died, the Deposed Former Emperor took the throne, and Faxing was transferred to Colonel of the Yue Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu died, the Deposed Former Emperor took the throne, and Faxing was promoted to Colonel of the Yue Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時太宰江夏王義恭錄尚書事，任同總己，而法興、尚之執權日久，威行內外，義恭積相畏服，至是懾憚尤甚。

translations.literal: At the time the Grand Mentor Prince of Jiangxia Liu Yigong recorded affairs of the Masters of Writing, his charge equal to holding all authority himself; yet Faxing and Shangzhi had wielded power for long, their might extending inside and out; Yigong had long feared and submitted to them, and now was especially cowed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Grand Mentor Prince of Jiangxia Liu Yigong recorded affairs of the Masters of Writing, his charge equal to holding all authority himself; yet Faxing and Shangzhi had wielded power for long, their might extending inside and out; Yigong had long feared and submitted to them, and now was especially cowed.

sentences.zh: 廢帝未親萬機，凡詔敕施為，悉決法興之手；

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor had not yet personally handled the myriad affairs of state; all edicts, orders, and measures were decided entirely in Faxing's hands;
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor had not yet personally handled the myriad affairs of state; all edicts, orders, and measures were decided entirely in Faxing's hands;

sentences.zh: 尚書中事無大小，專斷之。

translations.literal: within the Masters of Writing, matters great and small, he decided alone.
translations.idiomatic: within the Masters of Writing, he decided all matters great and small on his own.

sentences.zh: 顏師伯、義恭守空名而已。

translations.literal: Yan Shibo and Yigong kept empty titles, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shibo and Yigong kept empty titles, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 廢帝年已漸長，凶志轉成，欲有所為，法興每相禁制，每謂帝曰：「官所為如此，欲作營陽耶？」

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor was gradually growing older, his vicious intent taking shape; when he wished to act, Faxing always restrained him, saying each time to the emperor, "Your Majesty acts in this way—do you wish to become another Lord of Yingyang?"
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor was gradually growing older, his vicious intent taking shape; when he wished to act, Faxing always restrained him, saying each time to the emperor, "Your Majesty acts in this way—do you wish to become another Lord of Yingyang?"

sentences.zh: 帝意稍不能平。

translations.literal: The emperor's resentment gradually could not be contained.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's resentment gradually could not be contained.

sentences.zh: 所愛幸閹人華願兒有盛寵，賜與金帛無算，法興常加裁減，願兒甚恨之。

translations.literal: The favored eunuch Hua Yuan'er enjoyed great favor; gifts of gold and silk to him were beyond counting; Faxing often cut them back, and Yuan'er hated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The favored eunuch Hua Yuan'er enjoyed great favor; gifts of gold and silk to him were beyond counting; Faxing often cut them back, and Yuan'er hated him deeply.

sentences.zh: 帝常使願兒出入市里，察聽風謠，而道路之言，謂法興為真天子，帝為應天子。

translations.literal: The emperor often sent Yuan'er in and out of the market streets to listen for popular songs and rumors; on the roads people said that Faxing was the true Son of Heaven and the emperor the responsive Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often sent Yuan'er in and out of the market streets to listen for popular songs and rumors; on the roads people said that Faxing was the true Son of Heaven and the emperor the responsive Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 願兒因此告帝曰：「外間雲宮中有兩天子，官是一人，戴法興是一人。

translations.literal: Yuan'er therefore reported to the emperor, "Outside they say there are two Sons of Heaven in the palace—Your Majesty is one, Dai Faxing is one.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan'er therefore reported to the emperor, "Outside they say there are two Sons of Heaven in the palace—Your Majesty is one, Dai Faxing is one.

sentences.zh: 官在深宮中，人物不相接；

translations.literal: Your Majesty is deep within the inner palace and does not meet people face to face;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is deep within the inner palace and does not meet people face to face;

sentences.zh: 法興與太宰、顏、柳一體，吸習往來，門客恆有數百，內外士庶，莫不畏服之。

translations.literal: Faxing is one body with the Grand Mentor, Yan, and Liu, breathing and learning together in constant coming and going; his retainers are always several hundred; gentry and commoners inside and out, none do not fear and submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing moves as one with the Grand Mentor, Yan, and Liu, in constant association; his retainers always number several hundred; gentry and commoners inside and out all fear and submit to him.

sentences.zh: 法興是孝武左右，複久在宮闈，今將他人作一家，深恐此坐席非複官許。」

translations.literal: Faxing was at Xiaowu's side and has long been in the palace women's quarters; now he would make others into one household—I deeply fear this seat will no longer be Your Majesty's to keep."
translations.idiomatic: Faxing was at Emperor Xiaowu's side and has long been in the inner palace; now he would make others into one household—I deeply fear this seat will no longer be yours to keep."

sentences.zh: 帝遂發怒，免法興官，遣還田裏，仍複徙付遠郡，尋又於家賜死，時年五十二。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon grew angry, dismissed Faxing from office, and sent him back to his fields; then he was again transferred and consigned to a distant commandery; soon afterward he was granted death at home; he was fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon grew angry, dismissed Faxing from office, and sent him back to his fields; then he was again transferred to a distant commandery; soon afterward he was ordered to die at home; he was fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 法興臨死，封閉庫藏，使家人謹錄鑰牡。

translations.literal: As Faxing faced death, he sealed the storehouses and bade his household carefully record the keys.
translations.idiomatic: As Faxing faced death, he sealed the storehouses and bade his household carefully record the keys.

sentences.zh: 死一宿，又殺其二子，截法興棺，焚之，籍沒財物。

translations.literal: One night after his death his two sons were also killed; Faxing's coffin was split open and burned, and his goods were confiscated by register.
translations.idiomatic: One night after his death his two sons were also killed; Faxing's coffin was split open and burned, and his goods were confiscated by register.

sentences.zh: 法興能為文章，頗行於世。

translations.literal: Faxing could compose literary pieces, which circulated fairly widely in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing could compose literary pieces, which circulated fairly widely in his time.

sentences.zh: 死後，帝敕巢尚之曰：「吾纂承洪基，君臨萬國，推心勳舊，著於遐邇。

translations.literal: After his death the emperor commanded Chao Shangzhi, saying, "I have succeeded to the great foundation and rule the myriad realms; I have extended my heart to meritorious elders, manifest to far and near.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the emperor commanded Chao Shangzhi, saying, "I have succeeded to the great foundation and rule the myriad realms; I have extended my heart to meritorious elders, manifest to far and near.

sentences.zh: 不謂戴法興恃遇負恩，專作威福，冒憲黷貨，號令自由，積釁累愆，遂至於此。

translations.literal: I did not expect that Dai Faxing, relying on favor, betrayed grace, monopolized authority and blessings, violated statutes and trafficked in goods, issued commands at will, accumulated offenses and repeated faults, and so came to this.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect that Dai Faxing, relying on favor, betrayed grace, monopolized authority and blessings, violated statutes and trafficked in goods, issued commands at will, accumulated offenses and repeated faults, and so came to this.

sentences.zh: 卿等忠勤在事，吾乃具悉，但道路之言，異同紛糾，非唯人情駭愕，亦玄象違度，委付之旨，良失本懷。

translations.literal: You and the others have been loyal and diligent in your duties—I know this fully—but what is said on the roads is tangled in dispute; not only are people's hearts alarmed, the dark signs also depart from their measure; the intent of my commission has truly missed its original aim.
translations.idiomatic: You and the others have been loyal and diligent in your duties—I know this fully—but what is said on the roads is tangled in dispute; not only are people's hearts alarmed, the celestial signs also depart from their measure; the intent of my commission has truly missed its original aim.

sentences.zh: 吾今日親覽萬機，留心庶事，卿等宜竭誠盡力，以副所期。」

translations.literal: Today I personally review the myriad affairs of state and attend to common matters; you ought to exhaust your loyalty and strength to fulfill what is expected."
translations.idiomatic: Today I personally review the myriad affairs of state and attend to common matters; you ought to exhaust your loyalty and strength to fulfill what is expected."

sentences.zh: 尚之時為新安王子鸞撫軍中兵參軍、淮陵太守。

translations.literal: At the time Shangzhi was Staff Major of the Army for Prince of Xin'an Liu Luan's Pacification Army and Administrator of Huailing.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shangzhi was Staff Major of the Army for Prince of Xin'an Liu Luan's Pacification Army and Administrator of Huailing.

sentences.zh: 乃解舍人，轉為撫軍諮議參軍，太守如故。

translations.literal: He was then relieved of his Attendant post and transferred to Pacification Army Advisory Major, his administrator's post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was then relieved of his Attendant post and transferred to Pacification Army Advisory Major, retaining his post as Administrator.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始二年，詔曰：「故越騎校尉吳昌縣開國男戴法興，昔從孝武，誠勤左右，入定社稷，預誓河山。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi, Emperor Ming's edict said, "The late Colonel of the Yue Cavalry, Baron of Wuchang county who founded a state, Dai Faxing, formerly followed Xiaowu, loyal and diligent at his side, settled the altars of state, and shared the oath upon river and mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taishi, Emperor Ming's edict said, "The late Colonel of the Yue Cavalry, Baron of Wuchang county who founded a state, Dai Faxing, formerly followed Emperor Xiaowu, loyal and diligent at his side, settled the altars of state, and shared the oath upon river and mountain.

sentences.zh: 及出侍東儲，竭盡心力，嬰害凶悖，朕甚湣之。

translations.literal: When he went out to attend the Eastern Heir, he exhausted heart and strength; he met harm from vicious rebellion, and We deeply pity him.
translations.idiomatic: When he went out to attend the Eastern Heir, he exhausted heart and strength; he met harm from vicious rebellion, and We deeply pity him.

sentences.zh: 可追複削注，還其封爵。」

translations.literal: His struck entries may be posthumously restored and his enfeoffment returned."
translations.idiomatic: His struck entries may be posthumously restored and his enfeoffment returned."

sentences.zh: 有司奏以法興孫靈珍襲封。

translations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized that Faxing's grandson Lingzhen should inherit the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices memorialized that Faxing's grandson Lingzhen should inherit the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「法興小人，專權豪姿，雖虐主所害，義由國討，不宜複貪人之封，封爵可停。」

translations.literal: Another edict said, "Faxing was a petty man who monopolized power in arrogant fashion; though the tyrannical ruler harmed him, righteousness lay with the state's punishment—he ought not again to enjoy another man's enfeoffment; the title and rank may be suspended."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, "Faxing was a petty man who monopolized power in arrogant fashion; though the tyrannical ruler harmed him, righteousness lay with the state's punishment—he ought not again to enjoy another man's enfeoffment; the title and rank may be suspended."

sentences.zh: 太宗初，複以尚之兼中書通事舍人、南清河太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign, Shangzhi was again made concurrent Palace Secretariat Communications Attendant and Administrator of Southern Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign, Shangzhi was again made concurrent Palace Secretariat Communications Attendant and Administrator of Southern Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷中書侍郎，太守如故。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Palace Secretariat Gentleman, his administrator's post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to Palace Secretariat Gentleman, retaining his post as Administrator.

sentences.zh: 未拜，改除前軍將軍，太守如故，侍太子于東宮。

translations.literal: Before he took office he was reassigned as General of the Van, his administrator's post unchanged, attending the crown prince in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took office he was reassigned as General of the Van, retaining his post as Administrator, attending the crown prince in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 晉安王子勳平後，以軍守管內，封邵陵縣男，食邑四百戶，固辭不受。

translations.literal: After Prince of Jin'an Liu Zixun was pacified, for guarding the commandery by military authority he was enfeoffed as Baron of Shaoling county with a fief of four hundred households; he firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince of Jin'an Liu Zixun was pacified, for guarding the commandery by military authority he was enfeoffed as Baron of Shaoling county with a fief of four hundred households; he firmly declined and did not accept.

sentences.zh: 轉黃門侍郎，出為新安太守，病卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, went out as Administrator of Xin'an, and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, went out as Administrator of Xin'an, and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 戴明寶，南東海丹徒人也。

translations.literal: Dai Mingbao was a man of Dantu in Southern Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Mingbao was a native of Dantu in Southern Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 亦曆員外散騎侍郎，給事中。

translations.literal: He also served as Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 世祖世，帶南清河太守。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaowu's reign he held the concurrent post of Administrator of Southern Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xiaowu's reign he held the concurrent post of Administrator of Southern Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即阼，權任悉歸法興，而明寶輕矣，以為宣威將軍、南東莞太守。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Former Emperor took the throne, power and commission all passed to Faxing, and Mingbao was slighted, appointed General Who Displays Might and Administrator of Southern Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Former Emperor took the throne, power and commission all passed to Faxing, and Mingbao was slighted, appointed General Who Displays Might and Administrator of Southern Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 景和末，增邑百戶。

translations.literal: At the end of Jinghe his fief was increased by a hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jinghe era his fief was increased by a hundred households.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，天下反叛，軍務煩擾，以明寶舊人，屢經戎事，複委任之，以為前軍將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign the realm rebelled and military affairs were vexed and pressing; because Mingbao was an old associate who had often seen military service, he was again entrusted and made General of the Van.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign the realm rebelled and military affairs were vexed and pressing; because Mingbao was an old associate who had often seen military service, he was again entrusted and made General of the Van.

sentences.zh: 事平，遷宣威將軍、晉陵太守，進爵為侯，增邑四百戶。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was transferred to General Who Displays Might and Administrator of Jinling, advanced in rank to Marquis, with his fief increased by four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs were settled he was transferred to General Who Displays Might and Administrator of Jinling, advanced in rank to Marquis, with his fief increased by four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 泰始三年，坐參掌戎事，多納賄貨，削增封官爵，系尚方，尋被宥。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi, for participating in military affairs and accepting many bribes, his added enfeoffment, office, and rank were struck; he was imprisoned in the Imperial Workshop, and soon pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taishi, for participating in military affairs and accepting many bribes, his added enfeoffment, office, and rank were struck; he was imprisoned in the Imperial Workshop, and soon pardoned.

sentences.zh: 複為安陸太守，加甯朔將軍，遊擊、驍騎將軍，武陵內史，宣城太守，順帝驃騎司馬。

translations.literal: He was again made Administrator of Anlu, with the additional title General Who Pacifies the North; then General Who Roams in Attack, General of Valiant Cavalry, Interior Minister of Wuling, Administrator of Xuancheng, and Chief of Staff to the Fast Cavalry of Emperor Shun.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Administrator of Anlu, with the additional title General Who Pacifies the North; then General Who Roams in Attack, General of Valiant Cavalry, Interior Minister of Wuling, Administrator of Xuancheng, and Chief of Staff to the Fast Cavalry of Emperor Shun.

sentences.zh: 升明初，年老，拜太中大夫，病卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shengming he was old and was appointed Grand Palace Grandee; he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shengming era he was old and was appointed Grand Palace Grandee; he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 武陵國典書令董元嗣，與法興、明寶等俱為世祖南中郎典簽。

translations.literal: Dong Yuansi, Director of Documents for Wuling kingdom, together with Faxing, Mingbao, and the rest had all been Registry Clerks of Emperor Xiaowu's Southern Palace Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yuansi, Director of Documents for Wuling kingdom, together with Faxing, Mingbao, and the rest had all been Registry Clerks of Emperor Xiaowu's Southern Palace Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三十年，奉使還都，值元兇弑立，遣元嗣南還，報上以徐湛之等反。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Yuanjia, on a mission returning to the capital, he encountered the Original Culprit's regicide and enthronement; he sent Yuansi back south to report to the emperor that Xu Chengzhi and others had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Yuanjia, on a mission returning to the capital, he encountered the Original Culprit's regicide and enthronement; he sent Yuansi back south to report to the emperor that Xu Chengzhi and others had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 上時在巴口，元嗣具言弑狀。

translations.literal: The emperor was then at Bokou; Yuansi set forth the regicide in full detail.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Bokou; Yuansi set forth the regicide in full detail.

sentences.zh: 上遣元嗣下都，奉表於劭。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Yuansi down to the capital to present a memorial to Shao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yuansi down to the capital to present a memorial to Shao.

sentences.zh: 既而上舉義兵，劭責元嗣，元嗣答曰：「始下，未有反謀。」

translations.literal: Soon afterward the emperor raised righteous troops; Shao blamed Yuansi, and Yuansi replied, "When I first went down, there was no plan of rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the emperor raised righteous troops; Shao blamed Yuansi, and Yuansi replied, "When I first went down, there was no plan of rebellion."

sentences.zh: 劭不信，備加考掠，不服，遂死。

translations.literal: Shao did not believe him, applied full torture, he would not confess, and so died.
translations.idiomatic: Shao did not believe him, applied full torture, he would not confess, and so died.

sentences.zh: 世祖事克，追贈員外散騎侍郎，使文士蘇寶生為之誄焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu's cause prevailed, he was posthumously granted Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and the literary man Su Baosheng was commissioned to compose his dirge.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu's cause prevailed, he was posthumously granted Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and the literary man Su Baosheng was commissioned to compose his dirge.

sentences.zh: 大明中，又有奚顯度者，南東海郯人也。

translations.literal: In the Daming era there was also Xi Xiandu, a man of Tan in Southern Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming era there was also Xi Xiandu, a native of Tan in Southern Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 官至員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He reached the office of Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the office of Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 世祖常使主領人功，而苛虐無道，動加捶撲，署雨寒雪，不聽暫休，人不堪命，或有自經死者。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu often had him oversee corvée labor; he was harsh and cruel beyond measure, constantly applying beatings; in rain, heat, cold, or snow he allowed no brief rest; men could not bear it, and some hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu often had him oversee corvée labor; he was harsh and cruel beyond measure, constantly applying beatings; in rain, heat, cold, or snow he allowed no brief rest; men could not bear it, and some hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 人役聞配顯度，如就刑戮。

translations.literal: When corvée laborers heard they were assigned to Xiandu, it was as if they were going to execution.
translations.idiomatic: When corvée laborers heard they were assigned to Xiandu, it was as if they were going to execution.

sentences.zh: 時建康縣考囚，或用方材壓額及踝脛，民間謠曰：「甯得建康壓額，不能受奚度拍。」

translations.literal: When Jiankang county interrogated prisoners, they sometimes used squared timbers to press the forehead and the ankles and shins; among the people a song said, "Better to have Jiankang press the forehead than to bear Xiandu's beatings."
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang county interrogated prisoners, they sometimes used squared timbers to press the forehead and ankles; among the people a song ran, "Better Jiankang pressing your brow than Xiandu's beatings."

sentences.zh: 又相戲曰：「勿反顧，付奚度。」

translations.literal: They also joked among themselves, "Do not look back—hand him over to Xiandu."
translations.idiomatic: They also joked, "Don't look back—hand him to Xiandu."

sentences.zh: 其酷暴如此。

translations.literal: His cruelty and violence were such.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his cruelty and violence.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝嘗戲雲：「顯度刻虐，為百姓所疾，比當除之。」

translations.literal: The Deposed Former Emperor once jested, "Xiandu is harsh and cruel and is hated by the common people; he should soon be removed."
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Former Emperor once jested, "Xiandu is harsh and cruel and hated by the people—he ought to be removed soon."

sentences.zh: 左右因倡「諾」。

translations.literal: Those at his side thereupon cried "Agreed!"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants thereupon cried "Agreed!"

sentences.zh: 即日宣旨殺焉。

translations.literal: That very day an edict was proclaimed and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: That very day an edict was issued and he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 時人比之孫皓殺岑昏。

translations.literal: People of the time compared this to Sun Hao's killing of Cen Hun.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time compared this to Sun Hao's execution of Cen Hun.

sentences.zh: 徐爰，字長玉，南琅邪開陽人也。

translations.literal: Xu Ai, styled Changyu, was a man of Kaiyang in Southern Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ai, styled Changyu, was a native of Kaiyang in Southern Langye commandery.

sentences.zh: 本名瑗，後以與傅亮父同名，改為爰。

translations.literal: His original name was Yuan; later, because it was the same as Fu Liang's father's name, he changed it to Ai.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Yuan; later, because it matched Fu Liang's father's name, he changed it to Ai.

sentences.zh: 初為晉琅邪王大司馬府中典軍，從北征。

translations.literal: At first he was Central Army Officer in the Grand Marshal's headquarters of Prince of Langye of Jin, and followed the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as Central Army Officer in the Grand Marshal's staff of the Prince of Langye under Jin, and joined the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 微密有意理，為高祖所知。

translations.literal: Subtle and meticulous, with thoughtful principles, he came to the Founding Emperor's notice.
translations.idiomatic: Subtle and thoughtful in his reasoning, he came to the Founding Emperor's notice.

sentences.zh: 少帝在東宮，入侍左右。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor was in the Eastern Palace, he entered to attend at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor was in the Eastern Palace, he entered service at his side.

sentences.zh: 太祖初，又見親任，曆治吏勞，遂至殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wen's reign he was again treated with intimacy and trust; passing through duties governing clerks and labor, he reached Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Wen's reign he was again treated with intimacy and trust; after successive posts governing clerks and labor, he rose to Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十二年，轉南台侍御史，始興王浚後軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to Attending Censor of the Southern Terrace and Rear Army of Prince Shixing Liu Jun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to Attending Censor of the Southern Terrace and served as Rear Army officer to Prince Shixing Liu Jun.

sentences.zh: 複侍太子于東宮，遷員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He again attended the crown prince in the Eastern Palace and was promoted to Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He again attended the crown prince in the Eastern Palace and was promoted to Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 太祖每出軍行師，常懸授兵略。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Wen went out with armies on campaign, he was often sent instructions on military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Wen took the field, Ai was often entrusted with military instructions from headquarters.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，重遣王玄謨等北伐，配爰五百人，隨軍向確磝，銜中旨，臨時宣示。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Wang Xuemo and others were again sent north; Ai was assigned five hundred men, followed the army toward Quejiao, bore the central command, and proclaimed it on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year Wang Xuemo and others were again sent on the northern campaign; Ai was given five hundred men, followed the army to Quejiao, bore the central command, and proclaimed it on the spot.

sentences.zh: 世祖至新亭，大將軍江夏王義恭南奔，爰時在殿內，誑劭追義恭，因得南走。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting, the Grand General Prince of Jiangxia Liu Yigong fled south; Ai was then inside the hall, deceived Shao into pursuing Yigong, and thereby escaped south.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting, the Grand General Prince of Jiangxia Liu Yigong fled south; Ai was inside the hall, tricked Shao into pursuing Yigong, and thus escaped south.

sentences.zh: 時世祖將即大位，軍府造次，不曉朝章。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xiaowu was about to take the great throne; the army headquarters was in haste and did not understand court regulations.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Xiaowu was about to take the throne; the army headquarters was in disarray and did not understand court ritual.

sentences.zh: 爰素諳其事，既至，莫不喜說，以兼太常丞，撰立儀注。

translations.literal: Ai had long been versed in such matters; when he arrived, none were not delighted; he was made concurrent Vice Director of the Grand Chamberlain and drafted ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Ai had long been versed in such matters; when he arrived, everyone was delighted; he was made concurrent Vice Director of the Grand Chamberlain and drafted ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 孝建初，補尚書水部郎，轉為殿中郎，兼右丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian he was appointed Gentleman of the Masters of Writing for Water Works, transferred to Palace Gentleman, and concurrently Vice Director on the right.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xiaojian era he was appointed Gentleman of the Masters of Writing for Water Works, then transferred to Palace Gentleman and made concurrent Vice Director on the right.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年，索虜寇邊，詔問群臣防禦之策，爰議曰：

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian the northern barbarians raided the borders; an edict asked the ministers for policies of defense; Ai submitted his opinion, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaojian the northern barbarians raided the borders; an edict asked the ministers for defense policies; Ai submitted his opinion, saying:

sentences.zh: 詔旨「虜犯邊塞，水陸遼遠，孤城危棘，複不可置」。

translations.literal: The edict's intent: "The barbarians violate the border passes; by water and land the distance is vast; isolated cities are perilously threatened, and moreover cannot be abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "The barbarians violate the border passes; by water and land the distance is vast; isolated cities stand in peril, and moreover cannot be abandoned."

sentences.zh: 臣以戎虜倡狂，狡焉滋廣，列卒擬候，伺覘間隙，不勞大舉，終莫永寧。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that the barbarian raiders are wildly arrogant, cunning and ever spreading; they array troops to watch and spy out openings; without a great campaign there will never be lasting peace.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that the barbarian raiders are wildly arrogant and ever more cunning; they array troops to watch and spy out openings; without a major campaign there will never be lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 然連于千里，費固巨萬，而中興造創，資儲未積，是以齊斧徘徊，朔氣稽掃。

translations.literal: Yet the line extends a thousand li, and expense is surely in the tens of thousands; the restoration has just been founded and stores are not yet accumulated—hence the axe of punishment hesitates and the northern winds delay their sweeping.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the frontier stretches a thousand li and expense runs to tens of thousands; the restoration has just been founded and stores are not yet accumulated—hence punitive campaigns hesitate and northern threats linger uncleared.

sentences.zh: 今皇運洪休，靈威遐懾，蠢爾遺燼，懼在誅剪，思肆蜂蠆，以表有餘，雖不敢深入濟、沛，或能草竊邊塞。

translations.literal: Now the imperial fortune is grand and blessed, numinous might awes the distant; these witless embers fear execution and extinction, yet think to unleash hornets and scorpions to show they still have strength; though they dare not deeply enter Ji and Pei, they may yet raid the border passes in scattered bands.
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial fortune is grand and blessed, numinous might awes the distant; these witless embers fear execution, yet think to stir up trouble to show they still have strength; though they dare not push deep into Ji and Pei, they may yet raid the border in scattered bands.

sentences.zh: 羽林鞭長，太倉遙阻，救援之日，勢不相及。

translations.literal: The Palace Guard's whip is long, the Grand Granary far blocked—the day rescue is needed, force cannot reach in time.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Guard is far away, the Grand Granary remote—when rescue is needed, help cannot arrive in time.

sentences.zh: 且當使緣邊諸戍，練卒嚴城，凡諸督統，聚糧蓄田，籌計資力，足相抗擬。

translations.literal: Moreover, the border garrisons ought to drill troops and fortify cities; all commanders should gather grain and store up fields, calculating resources and strength sufficient to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, border garrisons ought to drill troops and fortify cities; all commanders should gather grain and open fields, calculating resources sufficient to resist them.

sentences.zh: 小鎮告警，大督電赴，塢壁邀斷，州郡犄角，儻有自送，可使匹馬不反。

translations.literal: When a small post raises the alarm, the great commander rushes like lightning; walled strongholds intercept and cut off, provinces and commanderies support each other like horns—if they come of their own accord, not a single horse need return.
translations.idiomatic: When a small post raises the alarm, the great commander rushes like lightning; walled strongholds intercept and cut off, provinces and commanderies support each other—if they come on their own, not a single horse need return.

sentences.zh: 詔旨「胡騎倏忽，抄暴無漸，出耕見虜，野粒資寇，比及少年，軍實無擬，江東根本，不可俱竭，宜立何方，可以相贍？」

translations.literal: The edict's intent: "Hu horsemen strike suddenly; their raids and violence have no gradual pattern; going out to plow one meets the barbarians; grain in the fields feeds the enemy; by the time the young men return, military stores cannot be gathered; the foundation of Jiangdong cannot be wholly drained—what method should be established to sustain one another?"
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Hu horsemen strike suddenly; their raids have no pattern; farmers going out to plow meet the enemy; grain in the fields feeds the raiders; by the time the young return, military stores cannot be gathered; Jiangdong's foundation cannot be wholly drained—what method can sustain the realm?"

sentences.zh: 臣以為方鎮所資，實宜且田且守，若使堅壁而春墾輟耕，清野而秋登莫擬，私無生業，公成虛罄，遠引根本，二三非宜。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that what the frontier commands rely on is truly to farm while defending; if one holds fast within walls and spring plowing ceases, clears the countryside and autumn harvest cannot be reckoned, private livelihoods vanish, public stores are emptied, and the distant foundation is drawn upon—such two or three courses are not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that frontier commands should farm while defending; if walls are held fast and spring plowing stops, if the countryside is cleared and autumn harvest fails, private livelihoods vanish and public stores empty—the distant foundation is drained; such courses are not fitting.

sentences.zh: 救之之術，唯在盡力防衛，來必拒戰，去則邀躡，據險保隘，易為首尾。

translations.literal: The method of rescue lies solely in defending with full force: when they come, refuse battle; when they leave, pursue and harass; hold perilous passes and guard narrow defiles—it is easy to coordinate head and tail.
translations.idiomatic: The method of rescue lies solely in defending with full force: when they come, meet them in battle; when they leave, pursue and harass; hold perilous passes and guard defiles—head and tail can easily coordinate.

sentences.zh: 胡馬既退，則民豐稟實，比及三載，可以長驅。

translations.literal: Once the Hu horses withdraw, the people will be rich in grain and stores; within three years one may drive far in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Hu horses withdraw, the people will be rich in grain and stores; within three years one may drive far in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 詔旨「賊之所向，本無前謀，兵之所進，亦無定所。

translations.literal: The edict's intent: "Where the bandits aim, there was originally no prior plan; where troops advance, there is likewise no fixed place.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Where the bandits aim, there was no prior plan; where troops advance, there is no fixed place.

sentences.zh: 比歲戎戍，倉庫多虛，先事聚眾，則消費糧粟，敵至倉卒，又無以相應。」

translations.literal: In recent years border garrisons have left granaries largely empty; gathering masses beforehand consumes grain and millet; when the enemy arrives suddenly, there is again nothing with which to respond."
translations.idiomatic: In recent years border garrisons have left granaries empty; gathering masses beforehand consumes grain; when the enemy arrives suddenly, there is nothing with which to respond."

sentences.zh: 臣以為推鋒前討，大須資力，據本應末，不俟多眾。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that driving the vanguard forward to attack greatly requires resources and strength; holding the root to meet the branch does not await many troops.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that driving the vanguard forward to attack requires great resources; holding the root to meet the branch does not require massing huge armies.

sentences.zh: 今寇無傾國豕突，列城勢足脣齒，養卒得勇，所任得才，臨事而懼，應機無失，豈煩空聚兵眾，以待未然。

translations.literal: Now the raiders have no whole-realm swine-rush; the ranked cities' strength is enough for lip-and-tooth mutual aid; training troops yields courage, appointing the right men yields talent; facing affairs with caution, responding to opportunity without error—why trouble to gather armies in vain to await what has not yet happened?
translations.idiomatic: Now the raiders cannot overrun the realm; the ranked cities support one another like lip and teeth; trained troops gain courage, the right appointees gain talent; facing affairs with caution and responding without error—why gather armies in vain to await what has not happened?

sentences.zh: 詔旨「戎狄貪婪，唯利是規，不挫凶圖，奸志歲結。」

translations.literal: The edict's intent: "The barbarians are greedy and plot only profit; if their vicious designs are not broken, treacherous intent knots year by year."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "The barbarians are greedy and plot only profit; if their vicious designs are not broken, treacherous intent grows year by year."

sentences.zh: 臣以為不擊則必侵掠，侵掠不已，則民失農桑；

translations.literal: Your servant holds that if they are not struck they will surely raid; if raiding does not cease, the people lose farming and sericulture;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that if they are not struck they will surely raid; if raiding does not cease, the people lose farming and sericulture;

sentences.zh: 農桑不收，則王戍不立，為立之方，擊之為要。

translations.literal: if farming and sericulture are not gathered, royal garrisons cannot stand; the method of establishing them is to strike—attack is essential.
translations.idiomatic: if farming and sericulture fail, royal garrisons cannot stand; the way to establish them is to strike—attack is essential.

sentences.zh: 詔旨「若令邊地歲驚，公私失業，經費困於遙輸，遠圖決無遂事，寢弊贊略，逆應有方」。

translations.literal: The edict's intent: "If the borderlands are alarmed year after year, public and private lose their livelihoods, expenses are strained by distant transport, long-range plans surely cannot succeed, growing weakness hampers strategy—there should be a method to meet the enemy in reverse."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "If the borderlands are alarmed year after year, public and private lose livelihoods, expenses strain distant transport, long-range plans cannot succeed, growing weakness hampers strategy—there should be a method to meet the enemy."

sentences.zh: 臣以為威虜之方，在於積粟塞下。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that the method of awing the barbarians lies in accumulating grain below the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that the way to awe the barbarians lies in accumulating grain below the passes.

sentences.zh: 若使邊民失業，列鎮寡儲，非唯無以遠圖，亦不能制其侵抄。

translations.literal: If border people lose their livelihoods and the ranked commands have scant stores, not only is there no means for distant plans, but one cannot restrain their raids either.
translations.idiomatic: If border people lose livelihoods and frontier commands have scant stores, not only can there be no long-range plans, but raids cannot be restrained either.

sentences.zh: 今當使小戍制其始寇，大鎮赴其入境，一被毒手，便自吹齏鳥逝矣。

translations.literal: Now small garrisons should check their first raids, great commands should rush when they cross the border; once they taste a bitter blow, they will scatter like blown chaff and birds in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Now small garrisons should check their first raids, great commands should rush when they cross the border; once they taste defeat, they will scatter like chaff before the wind.

sentences.zh: 尋即真，遷左丞。

translations.literal: Soon he took regular office and was transferred to Vice Director on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he took regular office and was promoted to Vice Director on the left.

sentences.zh: 先是元嘉中，使著作郎何承天草創國史。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Yuanjia, Gentleman Author He Chengtian was ordered to draft the founding of the dynastic history.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Yuanjia era, Gentleman Author He Chengtian was ordered to draft the dynastic history.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，又使奉朝請山謙之、南台禦史蘇寶生踵成之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, Court Gentleman Shan Qianzhi and Censor of the Southern Terrace Su Baosheng were again ordered to continue and complete it.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, Court Gentleman Shan Qianzhi and Censor of the Southern Terrace Su Baosheng were ordered to continue and complete it.

sentences.zh: 六年，又以爰領著作郎，使終其業。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Ai was again put in charge as Gentleman Author and ordered to finish the work.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Ai was put in charge as Gentleman Author and ordered to finish the work.

sentences.zh: 爰雖因前作，而專為一家之書。

translations.literal: Although Ai built on the earlier work, he made it exclusively his own book.
translations.idiomatic: Although Ai built on earlier work, he made it exclusively his own history.

sentences.zh: 上表曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞虞史炳圖，原光被之美，夏載昭策，先隨山之勤。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the histories of Yu blaze forth in their charts, tracing the beauty of light spread abroad; the records of Xia proclaim their policies, putting first the toil of following the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that the histories of Yu blaze forth in their charts, tracing how virtue spread abroad; the records of Xia proclaim their policies, putting first the toil of following the mountains.

sentences.zh: 天飛雖王德所至，終陟固有資田躍，神宗始於俾乂，上日兆於納揆。

translations.literal: Heaven's flight, though reached through kingly virtue, still ascends the end because there is foundation in field and leap; the divine ancestor began in assisting governance; the ascending day was foretold in receiving the regency.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate, though reached through kingly virtue, still ascends because there is foundation in effort; the divine ancestor began in assisting governance; the ascending day was foretold in receiving the regency.

sentences.zh: 其在《殷頌》，《長髮》玄王，受命作周，實唯雍伯，考行之盛則，振古之弘軌。

translations.literal: In the "Odes of Yin," in "Long Hair" the Dark King received the mandate and made Zhou—truly it was Lord Yong; examining the great norms of conduct, it shakes the ancient grand track.
translations.idiomatic: In the "Odes of Yin," in "Long Hair" the Dark King received the mandate and founded Zhou—it was truly Lord Yong; examining the great norms of conduct, it exemplifies the grand path of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 降逮二漢，亦同茲義，基帝創乎豐郊，紹祚本於昆邑。

translations.literal: Descending to the two Han, the meaning is likewise: the founding emperor was raised at Feng's outskirts; succession of the throne rooted in Kunyi.
translations.idiomatic: Descending to the two Han, the meaning is the same: the founding emperor rose at Feng's outskirts; the succession rooted in Kunyi.

sentences.zh: 魏以武命《國志》，晉以宣啟《陽秋》，明黃初非更姓之本，泰始為造物之末，又近代之令准，式遠之鴻規。

translations.literal: Wei took Martial's mandate for the "Records of the Realm"; Jin took Xuan's opening for the "Spring and Autumn"; Bright Huangchu was not the root of changing the surname; Supreme Primordial was the end of creating things—again the statutes of recent times, the great rule looking to the distant past.
translations.idiomatic: Wei took Cao Cao's mandate for the "Records of the Realm"; Jin took Sima Yi's opening for the "Spring and Autumn"; the Ming Huangchu era was not the root of changing the surname; the Taishi era was the end of creating the dynasty—again the statutes of recent times, the great rule looking to antiquity.

sentences.zh: 典謨緬邈，紀傳成准，善惡具書，成敗畢記。

translations.literal: Canons and counsels stretch far and remote; annals and biographies form the standard; good and evil are fully written; success and failure completely recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Canons and counsels stretch into the distant past; annals and biographies form the standard; good and evil are fully written; success and failure completely recorded.

sentences.zh: 然餘分紫色，滔天泯夏，親所芟夷，而不序於始傳，涉、聖、卓、紹，煙起雲騰，非所誅滅，而顯冠乎首述，豈不以事先歸之前錄，功偕著之後撰。

translations.literal: Yet fractional purple usurpers, flooding heaven and extinguishing Xia, were personally cut down by him yet are not arranged in the opening biography; She, Sheng, Zhuo, and Shao rose like smoke and soared like clouds—not those he executed and destroyed—yet stand conspicuous at the head of the narrative—is it not because events first belong in the prior record and merit together is set down in the later compilation?
translations.idiomatic: Yet fractional purple usurpers who flooded heaven and extinguished Xia were personally cut down by him yet are not placed in the opening biography; She, Sheng, Zhuo, and Shao rose like smoke and clouds—not those he executed—yet stand at the head of the narrative—is it not because events first belong in the prior record and merit is set down in the later compilation?

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇宋承金行之澆季，鐘經綸之屯極，擁玄光以鳳翔，秉神符而龍舉，喿刂定鯨鯢，天人佇屬。

translations.literal: Bowingly considering that Great Song succeeded the Metal Phase's declining season, encountered the crisis extreme of ordering the realm, embraced dark radiance and soared like a phoenix, grasped the divine tally and rose like a dragon, settled whale and crocodile, heaven and man awaiting their attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Bowingly considering that Great Song succeeded the Metal Phase's declining age, encountered the crisis of ordering the realm, embraced dark radiance and soared like a phoenix, grasped the divine tally and rose like a dragon, settled whale and crocodile, heaven and man awaiting their lord.

sentences.zh: 晉祿數終，上帝臨宋，便應奄膺珣宇，對越神工，而恭服勤於三分，讓德邁於不嗣，其為巍巍蕩蕩，赫赫明明，曆觀逖聞，莫或斯等。

translations.literal: Jin's fortune reached its term; the Supreme Lord descended upon Song and ought to have embraced the jade realm and faced the divine work—yet he served diligently in the threefold division and yielded virtue surpassing refusal of succession; how lofty and vast, how brilliant and clear—surveying distant ages and far-heard fame, none equals this.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's fortune reached its term; the Supreme Lord descended upon Song and ought to have embraced the realm and faced heaven—yet he served diligently in the threefold division and yielded virtue surpassing refusal of succession; how lofty and vast, how brilliant and clear—surveying distant ages, none equals this.

sentences.zh: 宜依銜書改文，登舟變號，起元義熙，為王業之始，載序宣力，為功臣之斷。

translations.literal: One ought to follow the inscribed text in revising the writing, board the boat and change the era name, begin the era in Yixi, taking it as the start of the royal enterprise, and record in sequence those who proclaimed their strength as the demarcation of meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: One ought to follow the inscribed text in revising the writing, board the boat and change the era name, begin the era in Yixi as the start of the royal enterprise, and record in sequence those who proclaimed their strength as the line of meritorious ministers.

sentences.zh: 其偽玄纂竊，同於新莽，雖靈武克殄，自詳之晉錄。

translations.literal: The false Xuan's usurped seizure is the same as Xin Mang's; though Spirit Martial destroyed them, let it be detailed in Jin's records.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan's usurped seizure is the same as Wang Mang's; though the Spirit Martial campaign destroyed them, let it be detailed in Jin's records.

sentences.zh: 及犯命幹紀，受戮霸朝，雖揖禪之前，皆著之宋策。

translations.literal: As for those who violated fate and breached discipline, executed by the hegemonic court—even before the yielding of the mandate, all are recorded in Song's annals.
translations.idiomatic: As for those who violated fate and breached discipline, executed by the hegemonic court—even before the yielding of the mandate, all are recorded in Song's annals.

sentences.zh: 國典體大，方垂不朽，請外詳議，伏須遵承。

translations.literal: The state's canon is great in body and about to be handed down imperishable; I beg that it be debated in detail elsewhere; bowingly I await compliance.
translations.idiomatic: The state's canon is momentous and about to be handed down imperishable; I beg that it be debated in detail elsewhere; bowingly I await your compliance.

sentences.zh: 七年，爰遷遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Ai was transferred to General Who Roams in Attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Ai was transferred to General Who Roams in Attack.

sentences.zh: 其年，世祖南巡，權以本官兼尚書左丞，車駕還宮，罷。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Xiaowu toured south; Ai was provisionally given his present office concurrently as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the left; when the imperial carriage returned to the palace, the concurrent post was ended.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Xiaowu toured south; Ai was provisionally made concurrent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the left; when the imperial carriage returned to the palace, the concurrent post ended.

sentences.zh: 明年，又兼左丞，著作兼如故。

translations.literal: The next year he was again concurrent Vice Director on the left, his authorship concurrent as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was again concurrent Vice Director on the left, retaining his authorship post as before.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，營景寧陵，爰以本官兼將作大匠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu died, Jingning Mausoleum was built; Ai with his present office was made concurrent Grand Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu died, Jingning Mausoleum was built; Ai retained his present office and was made concurrent Grand Master of Works.

sentences.zh: 爰便僻善事人，能得人主微旨，頗涉書傳，尤悉朝儀。

translations.literal: Ai was clever at crooked ways and skilled at pleasing people, able to grasp the ruler's subtle intent; he ranged fairly through books and records and was especially versed in court ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Ai was clever at ingratiating himself and skilled at pleasing people, able to grasp the ruler's subtle intent; he ranged through books and records and was especially versed in court ritual.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初便入侍左右，預參顧問，既長於附會，又飾以典文，故為太祖所任遇。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia he entered to attend at the ruler's side and participated in consultation; skilled at attaching himself to others and adorning himself with canonical texts, he was therefore entrusted and favored by Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanjia he entered service at the ruler's side and participated in consultation; skilled at attaching himself to power and adorning himself with canonical texts, he was therefore entrusted and favored by Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 大明世，委寄尤重，朝廷大體儀注，非爰議不行。

translations.literal: In the Daming era his commission was especially weighty; great court ritual regulations would not proceed without Ai's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming era his commission was especially weighty; great court ritual regulations would not proceed without Ai's deliberation.

sentences.zh: 雖複當時碩學所解過人者，既不敢立異議，所言亦不見從。

translations.literal: Even when great scholars of the time whose understanding surpassed others dared not raise differing opinions, what they said was likewise not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Even when great scholars of the time whose understanding surpassed others dared not raise differing opinions, what they said was likewise not heeded.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，公除後，晉安王子勳侍讀博士咨爰宜習業與不？

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu died, after the public mourning period, Prince of Jin'an Liu Zixun's Lecturer Doctor inquired of Ai whether study was appropriate or not.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu died, after the public mourning period, Prince of Jin'an Liu Zixun's Lecturer Doctor inquired of Ai whether study was appropriate or not.

sentences.zh: 爰答：「居喪讀喪禮，習業何嫌。」

translations.literal: Ai replied, "While in mourning one reads mourning rites—what objection is there to continuing study?"
translations.idiomatic: Ai replied, "While in mourning one reads mourning rites—what objection is there to continuing study?"

sentences.zh: 少日，始安王子真博士又咨爰，爰曰：「小功廢業，三年喪何容讀書。」

translations.literal: A few days later Prince of Shian Liu Zizhen's Doctor again consulted Ai; Ai said, "For lesser merit mourning study is abandoned—in three-year mourning how can reading books be allowed?"
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Prince of Shian Liu Zizhen's Doctor again consulted Ai; Ai said, "For lesser merit mourning study is abandoned—in three-year mourning how can reading books be allowed?"

sentences.zh: 其專斷乖謬皆如此。

translations.literal: His arbitrary decisions and perverse errors were all like this.
translations.idiomatic: His arbitrary decisions and perverse errors were all like this.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝兇暴無道，殿省舊人，多見罪黜，唯爰巧於將迎，始終無迕。

translations.literal: The Deposed Former Emperor was vicious and violent beyond the Way; old men of the palace offices were mostly punished and dismissed—only Ai was clever at meeting and welcoming and from start to finish met no offense.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Former Emperor was vicious and violent beyond measure; old men of the palace offices were mostly punished and dismissed—only Ai was clever at meeting and welcoming and from start to finish met no offense.

sentences.zh: 誅群公後，以爰為黃門侍郎，領射聲校尉，著作如故。

translations.literal: After the great lords were executed, Ai was made Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, heading the Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound, his authorship as before.
translations.idiomatic: After the great lords were executed, Ai was made Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, heading the Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound, retaining his authorship post as before.

sentences.zh: 封吳平縣子，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Wuping county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Wuping county with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 寵待隆密，群臣莫二。

translations.literal: Favor and treatment were lofty and close; among the ministers none was second.
translations.idiomatic: Favor and treatment were lofty and intimate; among the ministers none was second to him.

sentences.zh: 帝每出行，常與沈慶之、山陰公主同輦，爰亦預焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went out, he was often in the same carriage with Shen Qingzhi and the Princess of Shanyin; Ai also took part.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went out, he was often in the same carriage with Shen Qingzhi and the Princess of Shanyin; Ai also rode with them.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，例削封，以黃門侍郎改領長水校尉，兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, enfeoffments were struck by precedent; as Gentleman of the Yellow Gates he was changed to head the Colonel of the Long River, concurrently Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the left.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, enfeoffments were struck by precedent; as Gentleman of the Yellow Gates he was changed to head the Colonel of the Long River and made concurrent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the left.

sentences.zh: 明年，除太中大夫，著作並如故。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Grand Palace Grandee, his authorship concurrent as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was appointed Grand Palace Grandee, retaining his authorship post as before.

sentences.zh: 爰秉權日久，上昔在籓，素所不說。

translations.literal: Ai had wielded power for long; the emperor, when formerly in his princedom, had never been pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ai had wielded power for long; the emperor, when formerly in his princedom, had never been pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 及景和世，屈辱卑約，爰禮敬甚簡，益銜之。

translations.literal: In the Jinghe era he was humiliated and kept low and abject; Ai's courtesy and respect were very slight, and the emperor harbored resentment all the more.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinghe era he was humiliated and kept low; Ai's courtesy was very slight, and the emperor harbored resentment all the more.

sentences.zh: 泰始三年，詔曰：

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taishi an edict said:

sentences.zh: 夫事君無禮，教道弗容；

translations.literal: Serving one's lord without propriety cannot be tolerated by the teaching of the Way;
translations.idiomatic: Serving one's lord without propriety cannot be tolerated by the teaching of the Way;

sentences.zh: 訕上炫己，人倫所棄。

translations.literal: slandering superiors and displaying oneself—human relations cast such men aside.
translations.idiomatic: slandering superiors and displaying oneself—human relations cast such men aside.

sentences.zh: 太中大夫徐爰拔跡廝猥，推斥饕逢，遂官參時望，門伍豪族，遷位轉榮，莫非超荷。

translations.literal: Grand Palace Grandee Xu Ai rose from base and vulgar tracks, pushed aside and met with gluttonous fortune, and thus his office joined the expectations of the age, his gates ranked with powerful clans; each transfer and promotion in glory was none but an excessive burden.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Palace Grandee Xu Ai rose from base and vulgar origins, pushed aside yet met with gluttonous fortune, and thus his office joined the expectations of the age, his gates ranked with powerful clans; each transfer and promotion was none but an excessive favor.

sentences.zh: 而諂側輕險，與性自俱，利口讒妄，自少及長，奉公在事，厘毫蔑聞，初無愧滿，常有窺進。

translations.literal: Yet fawning and crooked, light and dangerous, were joined with his nature from birth; sharp-tongued slander and falsehood from youth to age; in serving the public in office not a hair's breadth was heard of merit; from the first no shame or satiety, always peering to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fawning and crooked, light and dangerous, were joined with his nature; sharp-tongued slander from youth to age; in public office not a trace of merit was heard; from the first no shame, always peering to advance.

sentences.zh: 先朝嘗以芻輩之中，粗有學解，故得漸蒙驅策，出入兩宮。

translations.literal: The former court once considered that among the hay-like rabble he had rough learning and understanding, and so he was gradually driven and used, entering and leaving both palaces.
translations.idiomatic: The former court once considered that among the common rabble he had rough learning, and so he was gradually employed, entering and leaving both palaces.

sentences.zh: 太初偽立，盡心佞事，義師已震，方得南奔。

translations.literal: When the false Taichu was established, he devoted his heart to fawning service; only when the righteous army had already shaken did he flee south.
translations.idiomatic: When the false Taichu was established, he devoted his heart to fawning service; only when the righteous army had already risen did he flee south.

sentences.zh: 及孝武居統，唯極諂諛，附會承旨，專恣厥性，致使治政苛縱，興造乖法，損德害民，皆由此豎。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu held the succession, he was utterly fawning and flattering, attaching himself to carry out intent, indulging his nature alone, causing government to be harsh yet lax, constructions to violate law, virtue to be harmed and the people injured—all through this petty fellow.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu held the throne, he was utterly fawning, attaching himself to carry out intent, indulging his nature alone, causing government to be harsh yet lax, constructions to violate law, virtue to be harmed and the people injured—all through this petty fellow.

sentences.zh: 景和悖險，深相贊協，苟取偷存，罔顧節義，任算設數，取合人主，崎嶇奸矯，所志必從，故曆事七朝，白首全貴。

translations.literal: In Jinghe's perverse danger he deeply collaborated in praise, snatching survival by theft, heedless of integrity and righteousness, trusting schemes and setting numbers to suit the ruler's will, crooked and treacherous in every bend—what he aimed at was always followed; hence he served seven courts and kept full honor to white hair.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinghe's perverse danger he deeply collaborated, snatching survival, heedless of integrity, trusting schemes to suit the ruler's will, crooked in every bend—what he aimed at was always followed; hence he served seven courts and kept full honor to white hair.

sentences.zh: 自以體含德厚，識鑒機先，迷塗遂深，罔知革悟。

translations.literal: He considered himself to embody thick virtue and foresight in discerning opportunity; the mistaken path grew ever deeper, unaware of reform and awakening.
translations.idiomatic: He considered himself to embody thick virtue and foresight; the mistaken path grew ever deeper, unaware of reform.

sentences.zh: 朕撥亂反正，勳濟天下，靈祗助順，群逆必夷，況爰恩養，而無輸效，遂內挾異心，著于形跡，陽愚杜口，罔所陳聞，惰事緩文，庶申詭略。
