translations.literal: We have settled chaos and restored correctness, merit aiding the realm; numinous powers assist the compliant, all rebels will be leveled—how much more Ai, whom We nurtured in grace yet who renders no contribution; he then harbored a different heart within, manifest in his tracks, feigning stupidity and sealing his mouth, reporting nothing, lazy in affairs and slow in documents, wishing to carry out treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: We have settled chaos and restored correctness, merit aiding the realm; numinous powers assist the compliant, all rebels will be leveled—how much more Ai, whom We nurtured in grace yet who renders no contribution; he harbored a different heart within, manifest in his conduct, feigning stupidity and sealing his mouth, lazy in affairs and slow in documents, wishing to carry out treacherous designs.

sentences.zh: 當今朝列賢彥，國無佞邪，而秉心弗純，累蠹時政。

translations.literal: Now the court ranks have worthy men; the state has no fawning evil—yet he holds an impure heart and repeatedly harms current government.
translations.idiomatic: Now the court ranks have worthy men; the state has no fawning evil—yet he holds an impure heart and repeatedly harms current government.

sentences.zh: 以其自告之辰，用賜歸老之職，榮禮優崇，寧非號饕過。

translations.literal: Because of the day he himself reported in, We granted the office of returning in age; honor and ritual were lofty and exalted—was this not called excessive gluttony of favor?
translations.idiomatic: Because of the day he himself reported in, We granted the office of returning in age; honor and ritual were lofty and exalted—was this not excessive favor?

sentences.zh: 不謂潛怨斥外，進競不已，勤言托意，觸遇斯發。

translations.literal: We did not expect hidden resentment after being cast out, advancement and rivalry unceasing, diligent words carrying hidden intent—when touched, it flared forth.
translations.idiomatic: We did not expect hidden resentment after being cast out, rivalry unceasing, diligent words carrying hidden intent—when touched, it flared forth.

sentences.zh: 小人之情，雖所先照，猶許其當改，未忍加法。

translations.literal: The feelings of a petty man, though foreseen, were still allowed room to reform; We could not bear to apply the law.
translations.idiomatic: The feelings of a petty man, though foreseen, were still allowed room to reform; We could not bear to apply the law.

sentences.zh: 遂恃朕仁弘，必永容貸。

translations.literal: He thereupon relied on Our benevolence and breadth, certain of eternal pardon.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon relied on Our benevolence, certain of eternal pardon.

sentences.zh: 昨因觴宴，肆意譏毀，謂制詔所為，皆資傍說。

translations.literal: Yesterday at a goblet feast he wantonly ridiculed and slandered, saying that everything done in drafting edicts relied on others' counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday at a banquet he wantonly mocked and slandered, claiming that every edict issued had been fed by others' gossip.

sentences.zh: 又宰輔無斷，朝要非才，恃老與舊，慢戾斯甚。

translations.literal: He also said the chief ministers lacked resolve and the court's key posts lacked talent; trusting in his age and seniority, his insolence and perversity were extreme.
translations.idiomatic: He also declared that the chief ministers were indecisive, that key court posts went to men without talent, and that relying on age and long tenure he had grown insolent beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 比邊難未靜，安眾以惠，戎略是務，政網從簡，故得使此小物，乘寬自縱。

translations.literal: Recently border troubles have not yet settled; We seek to settle the masses through kindness, give priority to military strategy, and simplify the governmental net—thus this petty creature was allowed to take advantage of Our lenience and indulge himself.
translations.idiomatic: Because border troubles had not yet subsided, We sought to reassure the people with kindness, give priority to military affairs, and keep governance light—thus this petty man was permitted to exploit Our lenience and run wild.

sentences.zh: 乃合投畀豺虎，以清王猷，但朽悴將盡，不足窮法，可特原罪，徙付交州。

translations.literal: It would be fitting to cast him to jackals and tigers to clear the royal plan; but his decrepit frame is nearly spent, not worth exhausting the law upon. He may be specially pardoned and exiled to Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He deserved to be cast among jackals and tigers to purge the royal design; yet his withered frame was nearly spent, not worth pursuing to the full letter of the law. We specially pardoned his offense and exiled him to Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 爰既行，又詔曰：「八議緩罪，舊在一條；

translations.literal: After Ai had departed, another edict said: "The Eight Deliberations and commuted punishments were formerly in one statute;
translations.idiomatic: After Ai had set out, another edict said: "The Eight Deliberations and commuted punishments were formerly set forth in a single statute;

sentences.zh: 五刑所抵，耆必加貸。

translations.literal: for punishments under the Five Punishments, the aged must receive additional leniency.
translations.idiomatic: for offenses under the Five Punishments, the aged must receive additional clemency.

sentences.zh: 徐爰前後釁跡，理無可申，廢棄海埵，實允國憲。

translations.literal: Xu Ai's offenses old and new offer no grounds for appeal; casting him out on the seacoast truly accorded with state law.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ai's offenses, past and present, offered no grounds for appeal; casting him out to the seacoast truly accorded with the law of the realm.

sentences.zh: 但蚤蒙朕識，曲矜愚朽，既經大宥，思沾殊渥。

translations.literal: But he long ago received Our notice and We bent to pity his foolish decrepitude; having already received a great pardon, We thought to bestow extraordinary grace.
translations.idiomatic: But he had long ago come to Our notice, and We bent to pity his foolish old age; having already granted a great pardon, We wished to bestow extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 可特除廣州統內郡。」

translations.literal: He may be specially appointed to an inner commandery of Guangzhou."
translations.idiomatic: He may be specially appointed to an inner commandery within Guangzhou."

sentences.zh: 有司奏以為宋隆太守。

translations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized that he be made Administrator of Songlong.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices memorialized that he be appointed Administrator of Songlong.

sentences.zh: 除命既下，爰已至交州，值刺史張牧病卒，土人李長仁為亂，悉誅北來流寓，無或免者。

translations.literal: Once the appointment order had been issued, Ai had already reached Jiaozhou. The Inspector Zhang Mu died of illness; the native Li Changren raised a rebellion and put to death all northerners who had come to sojourn there—not one escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Once the appointment order had been issued, Ai had already reached Jiaozhou. The provincial inspector Zhang Mu died of illness, and the local leader Li Changren raised a rebellion, executing every northerner who had settled there—not one was spared.

sentences.zh: 長仁素聞爰名，以智計誑誘，故得無患。

translations.literal: Changren had long heard of Ai's fame and used schemes to deceive and lure him, so Ai escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Changren had long heard of Ai's reputation and used cunning to deceive and win him over, so Ai escaped unscathed.

sentences.zh: 久之聽還，仍除南康郡丞。

translations.literal: After a long time he was permitted to return and was appointed Vice-Prefect of Nankang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was permitted to return and was appointed vice-prefect of Nankang commandery.

sentences.zh: 太宗崩，還京都，以爰為南濟陰太守，複除中散大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, Ai returned to the capital and was made Administrator of Nanjiyin; he was also reappointed Palace Grandee Without Specification.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, Ai returned to the capital, was made administrator of Nanjiyin, and was reappointed palace grandee without specification.

sentences.zh: 元徽三年，卒，時年八十二。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanhui he died, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanhui he died, at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 阮佃夫，會稽諸暨人也。

translations.literal: Ruan Dianfu was a native of Zhuji in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Dianfu was a native of Zhuji in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，出身為台小史。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era he first entered service as a minor clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanjia era he first entered service as a minor clerk of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太宗初出閣，選為主衣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming first left the palace quarters, Dianfu was selected as master of robes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming first left the palace quarters, he was selected to serve as master of robes.

sentences.zh: 世祖召還左右，補內監。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu recalled him to attend at his side and made him Inner Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu recalled him to attend at his side and appointed him inner supervisor.

sentences.zh: 永光中，太宗又請為世子師，甚見信待。

translations.literal: In the Yongguang era Emperor Ming again requested him as tutor to the heir apparent, and he was greatly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongguang era Emperor Ming again requested him as tutor to the heir apparent, and he enjoyed great trust and favor.

sentences.zh: 景和末，太宗被拘於殿內，住在秘書省，為帝所疑，大禍將至，惶懼計無所出。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jinghe era Emperor Ming was confined within the palace halls, lodging in the Secretariat, suspected by the emperor; great disaster was about to arrive, and in panic he could find no plan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jinghe era Emperor Ming was confined within the palace halls and lodged in the Secretariat, suspected by the Deposed Former Emperor; catastrophe was imminent, and in terror he could find no way out.

sentences.zh: 佃夫與王道隆、李道兒及帝左右琅邪淳于文祖謀共廢立。

translations.literal: Dianfu, together with Wang Daolong, Li Dao'er, and Chunyu Wenzu of Langye, who attended the emperor at his side, plotted jointly to depose and install.
translations.idiomatic: Dianfu, together with Wang Daolong, Li Dao'er, and Chunyu Wenzu of Langye, attendants at the emperor's side, plotted jointly to depose the ruler and install another.

sentences.zh: 時直閣將軍柳光世亦與帝左右蘭陵繆方盛、丹陽周登之有密謀，未知所奉。

translations.literal: At the time the General of Direct Attendance Liu Guangshi also had a secret plot with Miao Fangsheng of Lanling and Zhou Dengzhi of Danyang, attendants at the emperor's side, but they did not yet know whom they would support.
translations.idiomatic: At the time General of Direct Attendance Liu Guangshi also had a secret plot with Miao Fangsheng of Lanling and Zhou Dengzhi of Danyang, attendants at the emperor's side, though they had not yet decided whom to support.

sentences.zh: 登之與太宗有舊，方盛等乃使登之結佃夫，佃夫大說。

translations.literal: Dengzhi had old ties with Emperor Ming; Fangsheng and the others therefore had Dengzhi win over Dianfu, and Dianfu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhi had old ties with Emperor Ming, so Fangsheng and the others had him win over Dianfu, and Dianfu was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝立皇后，普暫徹諸王奄人，太宗左右錢藍生亦在其例。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor installed the empress, all eunuchs of the princes were generally temporarily withdrawn; Qian Lansheng, an attendant of Emperor Ming, was among them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor installed the empress, eunuchs serving the princes were generally withdrawn for the occasion; Qian Lansheng, an attendant of Emperor Ming, was among them.

sentences.zh: 事畢，未被遣，密使藍生候帝，慮事泄，藍生不欲自出，帝動止輒以告淳于文祖，令文祖報佃夫。

translations.literal: When the affair was finished he was not sent away; they secretly had Lansheng watch the emperor, fearing the matter would leak. Lansheng did not wish to go out himself; the emperor's every move was at once told to Chunyu Wenzu, who was to report to Dianfu.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was finished he was not sent away; they secretly had Lansheng watch the emperor, fearing the plot would leak. Lansheng did not wish to go out himself, so the emperor's every move was reported at once to Chunyu Wenzu, who in turn informed Dianfu.

sentences.zh: 時巫覡雲：「後堂有鬼。」

translations.literal: At the time a shaman said: "There is a ghost in the rear hall."
translations.idiomatic: At the time a shaman declared: "There is a ghost in the rear hall."

sentences.zh: 其夕，帝于竹林堂前，與巫共射之。

translations.literal: That evening the emperor, before the Bamboo Grove Hall, shot at it together with the shaman.
translations.idiomatic: That evening, before the Bamboo Grove Hall, the emperor shot at it together with the shaman.

sentences.zh: 建安王休仁等山陰主並從。

translations.literal: Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren, the Princess of Shanyin, and others all followed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren, the Princess of Shanyin, and others all accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 帝素不說寂之，見輒切齒。

translations.literal: The emperor had never been pleased with Shou Jizhi and gnashed his teeth whenever he saw him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had never liked Shou Jizhi and would gnash his teeth whenever he saw him.

sentences.zh: 寂之既與佃夫成謀，又慮禍至，抽刀前入；

translations.literal: Shou Jizhi, having completed his plot with Dianfu and fearing disaster was at hand, drew his sword and advanced;
translations.idiomatic: Shou Jizhi, having sealed his plot with Dianfu and fearing disaster was imminent, drew his sword and rushed forward;

sentences.zh: 薑產之隨其後，淳于文祖、繆方盛、周登之、富靈符、聶慶、田嗣、王敬則、俞道龍、宋逵之又繼進。

translations.literal: Jiang Chanzhi followed behind him, and Chunyu Wenzu, Miao Fangsheng, Zhou Dengzhi, Fu Lingfu, Nie Qing, Tian Si, Wang Jingze, Yu Daolong, and Song Kuizhi entered in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Chanzhi followed close behind, and Chunyu Wenzu, Miao Fangsheng, Zhou Dengzhi, Fu Lingfu, Nie Qing, Tian Si, Wang Jingze, Yu Daolong, and Song Kuizhi pressed in after them.

sentences.zh: 休仁聞行聲甚疾，謂休祐曰：「事作矣。」

translations.literal: Xiuren heard the footsteps very hurried and said to Xiuyou: "The deed is done."
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren heard the footsteps coming very fast and said to Xiuyou: "It has begun."

sentences.zh: 相隨奔景陽山。

translations.literal: They fled together to Jingyang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: They fled together toward Jingyang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 帝見寂之至，引弓射之，不中，乃走，寂之追而殞之。

translations.literal: When the emperor saw Jizhi arrive, he drew his bow and shot at him but missed; he then fled, and Jizhi pursued and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor saw Jizhi arrive, he drew his bow and shot at him but missed; he then fled, and Jizhi pursued and struck him down.

sentences.zh: 事定，宣令宿衛曰：「湘東王受太后令，除狂主。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, an order was proclaimed to the palace guards, saying: "The Prince of Xiangdong, acting on the empress dowager's command, has removed the mad ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, an order was proclaimed to the palace guards, saying: "The Prince of Xiangdong, acting on the empress dowager's command, has removed the mad emperor.

sentences.zh: 今已平定。」

translations.literal: All is now pacified."
translations.idiomatic: The realm is now pacified."

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，論功行賞，壽寂之封應城縣侯，食邑千戶；

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, merit was weighed and rewards given: Shou Jizhi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yingcheng county with a fief of one thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, merit was weighed and rewards dispensed: Shou Jizhi was enfeoffed as marquis of Yingcheng county with a fief of one thousand households;

sentences.zh: 姜產之汝南縣侯，佃夫建城縣侯，食邑八百戶。

translations.literal: Jiang Chanzhi was made Marquis of Runan county and Dianfu Marquis of Jiancheng county, each with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Chanzhi was made marquis of Runan county and Dianfu marquis of Jiancheng county, each with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 王道隆吳平縣侯，淳于文祖陽城縣侯，食邑各五百戶。

translations.literal: Wang Daolong was Marquis of Wuping county and Chunyu Wenzu Marquis of Yangcheng county, each with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Daolong was made marquis of Wuping county and Chunyu Wenzu marquis of Yangcheng county, each with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 李道兒新塗縣侯，繆方盛劉陽縣侯，周登之曲陵縣侯，食邑各四百戶。

translations.literal: Li Dao'er was Marquis of Xintu county, Miao Fangsheng Marquis of Liuyang county, and Zhou Dengzhi Marquis of Quling county, each with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dao'er was made marquis of Xintu county, Miao Fangsheng marquis of Liuyang county, and Zhou Dengzhi marquis of Quling county, each with a fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 富靈符惠懷縣子，聶慶建陽縣子，田嗣將樂縣子，王敬則重安縣子，俞道龍茶陵縣子，宋逵之零陵縣子，食邑各三百戶。

translations.literal: Fu Lingfu was made Viscount of Huihuai county, Nie Qing Viscount of Jianyang county, Tian Si Viscount of Jiangle county, Wang Jingze Viscount of Chong'an county, Yu Daolong Viscount of Chaling county, and Song Kuizhi Viscount of Lingling county, each with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lingfu was made viscount of Huihuai county, Nie Qing viscount of Jianyang county, Tian Si viscount of Jiangle county, Wang Jingze viscount of Chong'an county, Yu Daolong viscount of Chaling county, and Song Kuizhi viscount of Lingling county, each with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 佃夫遷南臺侍御史。

translations.literal: Dianfu was transferred to Attending Censor of the Southern Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Dianfu was transferred to the post of attending censor of the Southern Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 薛索兒渡淮為寇，山陽太守程天祚又反，佃夫與諸軍討之，破索兒，降天祚。

translations.literal: Xue Suo'er crossed the Huai to plunder, and the Administrator of Shanyang Cheng Tianzuo also rebelled; Dianfu joined the various armies in attacking them, defeated Suo'er, and received Tianzuo's surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Suo'er crossed the Huai to raid, and the administrator of Shanyang Cheng Tianzuo also rebelled; Dianfu joined the various armies in suppressing them, defeated Suo'er, and accepted Tianzuo's surrender.

sentences.zh: 遷龍驤將軍、司徒參軍，率所領南助赭圻，轉太子步兵校尉、南魯郡太守，侍太子于東宮。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of the Dragon Chariot and Staff Officer of the Minister of Education, leading his command south to aid Zhuchi; he was transferred to Colonel of Footsoldiers of the Heir Apparent and Administrator of Nanlu commandery, attending the heir apparent in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of the dragon chariot and staff officer of the minister of education, leading his troops south to aid Zhuchi; he was then transferred to colonel of footsoldiers of the heir apparent and administrator of Nanlu commandery, attending the heir apparent in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 太始四年，以破薛索兒功，增封二百戶，並前千戶；

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi, for his merit in defeating Xue Suo'er, his enfeoffment was increased by two hundred households, making one thousand in all;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taishi, for his merit in defeating Xue Suo'er, his fief was increased by two hundred households, bringing the total to one thousand;

sentences.zh: 以本官兼遊擊將軍，假甯朔將軍，與輔國將軍兼驍騎將軍孟次陽與二衛參員直。

translations.literal: holding his original office, he also served as General Who Scours the Regions, and was given the provisional rank of General Who Pacifies the North; together with the Assistant General Who Supports the State and Concurrent General of the Valiant Cavalry Meng Ciyang he shared duty with the two guards in regular attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Retaining his original office, he also served as general who scours the regions and was given the provisional rank of general who pacifies the north; together with assistant general who supports the state and concurrent general of the valiant cavalry Meng Ciyang he shared regular attendance duty with the two palace guards.

sentences.zh: 次陽字崇基，平昌安丘人也。

translations.literal: Ciyang, courtesy name Chongji, was a native of Anqiu in Pingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Ciyang, courtesy name Chongji, was a native of Anqiu in Pingchang commandery.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，為山陽王休祐驃騎參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he served as Staff Officer of the Rapid Cavalry under Prince of Shanyang Liu Xiuyou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taishi he served as staff officer of the rapid cavalry under Prince of Shanyang Liu Xiuyou.

sentences.zh: 薛安都子道標攻合肥，次陽擊破之，以功封攸縣子，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Xue Andu's son Daobiao attacked Hefei; Ciyang defeated him and for his merit was enfeoffed as Viscount of You county with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andu's son Daobiao attacked Hefei; Ciyang defeated him and, for his merit, was enfeoffed as viscount of You county with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 曆右軍、驃騎參軍；

translations.literal: He successively served as staff officer of the Right Army and of the Rapid Cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as staff officer of the Right Army and of the Rapid Cavalry;

sentences.zh: 六年，出為輔師將軍、兗州刺史，戍淮陰。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he went out as General Who Assists the Army and Inspector of Yan province, garrisoning Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was sent out as general who assists the army and inspector of Yan province, garrisoning Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 立北兗州，自此始也。

translations.literal: The establishment of Northern Yan province began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The establishment of Northern Yan province began at this time.

sentences.zh: 進號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Uplifts the Army.
translations.idiomatic: His title was advanced to general who uplifts the army.

sentences.zh: 元徽四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhui he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Yuanhui.

sentences.zh: 時佃夫、王道隆、楊運長並執權柄，亞於人主。

translations.literal: At the time Dianfu, Wang Daolong, and Yang Yunchang alike held the reins of power, second only to the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Dianfu, Wang Daolong, and Yang Yunchang alike held the reins of power, standing second only to the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 巢、戴大明之世方之蔑如也。

translations.literal: Compared to them, Chao and Dai at their height in the Daming era were utterly negligible.
translations.idiomatic: Even Chao and Dai at the height of their power in the Daming era were nothing beside them.

sentences.zh: 嘗值正旦應合朔，尚書奏遷元會，佃夫曰：「元正慶會，國之大禮，何不遷合朔日邪？」

translations.literal: Once when New Year's Day coincided with the new moon, the Masters of Writing memorialized to move the New Year's audience; Dianfu said: "The New Year's celebration is a great state rite—why not move the day of the new moon instead?"
translations.idiomatic: Once when New Year's Day coincided with the new moon, the Masters of Writing memorialized to postpone the New Year's audience; Dianfu said: "The New Year's celebration is a great state rite—why not move the new-moon day instead?"

sentences.zh: 其不稽古如此。

translations.literal: Such was his disregard for classical precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his ignorance of classical precedent.

sentences.zh: 大通貨賄，凡事非重賂不行。

translations.literal: He widely accepted bribes; nothing was done without heavy payment.
translations.idiomatic: He openly traded in bribes; nothing could be accomplished without a heavy payment.

sentences.zh: 人有餉絹二百匹，嫌少，不答書。

translations.literal: When someone sent him two hundred bolts of silk as a gift, he considered it too little and gave no reply.
translations.idiomatic: When someone sent him two hundred bolts of silk as a gift, he thought it too little and did not even send a reply.

sentences.zh: 宅舍園池，諸王邸第莫及。

translations.literal: His residences, gardens, and ponds—no princely mansion could match them.
translations.idiomatic: His houses, gardens, and ponds surpassed every princely mansion.

sentences.zh: 妓女數十，藝貌冠絕當時，金玉錦繡之飾，宮掖不逮也。

translations.literal: He had dozens of courtesans whose art and looks were unmatched in the age; their adornment in gold, jade, brocade, and embroidery surpassed even the palace women's.
translations.idiomatic: He kept dozens of courtesans whose talent and beauty were unmatched in the age; their adornment in gold, jade, brocade, and embroidery outshone even the palace women.

sentences.zh: 每制一衣，造一物，京邑莫不法效焉。

translations.literal: Whenever he had a garment made or an object crafted, the capital had none who did not imitate it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he had a garment made or an object crafted, everyone in the capital copied it.

sentences.zh: 於宅內開瀆，東出十許裏，塘岸整潔，泛輕舟，奏女樂。

translations.literal: Within his residence he opened a canal running more than ten li eastward; the dikes and banks were neatly kept, and he floated light boats while female musicians played.
translations.idiomatic: Within his residence he opened a canal extending more than ten li to the east; the dikes and banks were kept in perfect order, and he would float light boats while female musicians played.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人劉休嘗詣之，值佃夫出行，中路相逢，要休同反；

translations.literal: Liu Xiu, Secretariat Gentleman, once called on him; he happened to meet Dianfu going out, and they met on the road; Dianfu invited Xiu to return with him;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiu, a secretariat gentleman, once called on him and happened to meet Dianfu going out; they encountered each other on the road, and Dianfu invited Xiu to return with him;

sentences.zh: 就席，便命施設，一時珍羞，莫不畢備。

translations.literal: When they took their seats he at once ordered things set out—a feast of rare delicacies, none of which was not fully provided.
translations.idiomatic: Once they took their seats he at once ordered a spread laid out—a feast of rare delicacies, every one of them fully provided.

sentences.zh: 凡諸火劑，並皆始熟，如此者數十種。

translations.literal: All the hot dishes were only just cooked; there were dozens of such items.
translations.idiomatic: Every hot dish had only just finished cooking; there were dozens of items like this.

sentences.zh: 佃夫嘗作數十人饌，以待賓客，故造次便辦，類皆如此，雖晉世王、石，不能過也。

translations.literal: Dianfu would regularly prepare feasts for dozens of people to await guests; thus he could instantly prepare everything, all of this kind—nor even the Wangs and Shis of Jin could surpass it.
translations.idiomatic: Dianfu regularly kept feasts prepared for dozens of guests, so he could produce such a spread at a moment's notice; even the Wang and Shi clans of Jin could not have matched it.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，軍功既多，爵秩無序，佃夫僕從附隸，皆受不次之位。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, military merit was plentiful and ranks and titles were disordered; Dianfu's servants and attendants who attached themselves to him all received extraordinary appointments.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taishi, military merit was plentiful and ranks and titles were in disorder; the servants and attendants who attached themselves to Dianfu all received extraordinary appointments.

sentences.zh: 捉車人虎賁中郎，傍馬者員外郎。

translations.literal: The man who held his carriage became a Palace Guard Commandant of the Tiger Fang; the man who walked beside his horse became an Outside the Office Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: The man who held his carriage was made a palace guard commandant of the Tiger Fang, and the man who walked beside his horse was made an outside-the-office gentleman.

sentences.zh: 朝士貴賤，莫不自結，而矜傲無所降意，入其室者，唯吳興沈勃、吳郡張澹數人而已。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen high and low all attached themselves to him of their own accord, yet he was proud and condescending to all; those who entered his hall were only Shen Bo of Wuxing, Zhang Tan of Wu commandery, and a few others.
translations.idiomatic: Court gentlemen high and low all sought ties with him on their own, yet he was proud and would condescend to none; those admitted to his hall were only Shen Bo of Wuxing, Zhang Tan of Wu commandery, and a few others.

sentences.zh: 時廢帝倡狂，好出遊走，始出宮，猶整羽儀，引隊仗；

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was unrestrained and mad, fond of going out to wander; when he first left the palace he still arrayed feathered insignia and led an armed escort;
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor was wild and unrestrained and loved to go out roaming; when he first left the palace he still arrayed feathered insignia and led an armed escort;

sentences.zh: 俄而棄部伍，單騎與數人相隨，或出郊野，或入市廛，內外莫不懼憂。

translations.literal: But soon he would abandon the ranks and ride alone with a few companions, sometimes going to the suburbs and countryside, sometimes entering market streets—inside and outside the court none were free from fear and worry.
translations.idiomatic: But soon he would abandon his escort and ride alone with only a few companions, sometimes into the countryside, sometimes into the markets—inside and outside the court everyone lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 佃夫密與直閣將軍申伯宗、步兵校尉硃幼、于天寶謀共廢帝，立安成王。

translations.literal: Dianfu secretly plotted with General of Direct Attendance Shen Bozong, Colonel of Footsoldiers Zhu You, and Yu Tianbao jointly to depose the emperor and install the Prince of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dianfu secretly plotted with General of Direct Attendance Shen Bozong, Colonel of Footsoldiers Zhu You, and Yu Tianbao to depose the emperor and install the Prince of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 五年春，帝欲往江乘射雉。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year the emperor wished to go to Jiangcheng to shoot pheasants.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year the emperor wished to go to Jiangcheng to hunt pheasants.

sentences.zh: 帝每北出，常留隊仗在樂游苑前，棄之而去。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went north out of the city, he would regularly leave the armed escort before the Leyou Park and abandon them to go on.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went north out of the city, he would leave his armed escort before Leyou Park and abandon them to go on alone.

sentences.zh: 佃夫欲稱太后令喚隊仗還，閉城門，分人守石頭、東府，遣人執帝廢之，自為揚州刺史輔政。

translations.literal: Dianfu intended to proclaim the empress dowager's command to summon the escort back, close the city gates, divide men to hold Stone City and the Eastern Palace, send men to seize the emperor and depose him, and himself serve as regent as Inspector of Yang province.
translations.idiomatic: Dianfu intended to proclaim the empress dowager's command to recall the escort, close the city gates, assign men to hold Stone City and the Eastern Palace, seize the emperor and depose him, and himself serve as regent as inspector of Yang province.

sentences.zh: 與幼等已成謀，會帝不成向江乘，故其事不行。

translations.literal: He and Zhu You and the others had already completed the plot, but the emperor happened not to go to Jiangcheng, and so the affair did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhu You and the others had already finalized the plot, but the emperor happened not to go to Jiangcheng, and so the affair came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 于天寶因以其謀告帝，帝乃收佃夫、幼、伯宗于光祿外部，賜死。

translations.literal: Yu Tianbao thereupon reported the plot to the emperor; the emperor then seized Dianfu, You, and Bozong outside the Office of Imperial Household Supplies and granted them death.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tianbao thereupon reported the plot to the emperor; the emperor then seized Dianfu, Zhu You, and Shen Bozong outside the Office of Imperial Household Supplies and had them put to death.

sentences.zh: 佃夫、幼罪止身，其餘無所問。

translations.literal: The guilt of Dianfu and You extended only to their persons; the others were not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: The guilt of Dianfu and Zhu You was limited to their persons alone; no one else was investigated.

sentences.zh: 佃夫時年五十一。

translations.literal: Dianfu was then fifty-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Dianfu was fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 壽寂之，泰始初，以軍功增邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Shou Jizhi—at the beginning of Taishi, for military merit his fief was increased by two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taishi his fief was increased by two hundred households for military merit.

sentences.zh: 為羽林監，遷太子屯騎校尉，尋加甯朔將軍、南泰山太守。

translations.literal: He served as Colonel of the Forest of Feathers, was transferred to Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry of the Heir Apparent, and soon was also given the rank of General Who Pacifies the North and made Administrator of South Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: He served as colonel of the Forest of Feathers, was transferred to colonel of the garrison cavalry of the heir apparent, and soon was also given the rank of general who pacifies the north and made administrator of South Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 多納貨賄，請謁無窮，有一不從，切齒罵詈，常雲：「利刀在手，何憂不辦。」

translations.literal: He accepted many bribes; requests and petitions were endless; when any one was refused he gnashed his teeth and cursed, often saying: "With a sharp knife in hand, why worry that things cannot be done?"
translations.idiomatic: He accepted many bribes, and requests and petitions were endless; whenever one was refused he gnashed his teeth and cursed, often saying: "With a sharp knife in hand, why worry that anything cannot be done?"

sentences.zh: 鞭尉吏，斫邏將。

translations.literal: He flogged commandery assistants and hacked at patrol officers.
translations.idiomatic: He had commandery assistants flogged and patrol officers hacked down.

sentences.zh: 七年，為有司所奏，徙送越州，行至豫章，謀欲逃叛，乃殺之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was impeached by the responsible offices, was exiled and sent to Yue province; when he reached Yuzhang he plotted to flee and rebel, and so was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was impeached by the responsible offices and exiled to Yue province; when he reached Yuzhang he plotted to flee and rebel, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 薑產之，泰始初，以軍功增邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Jiang Chanzhi—at the beginning of Taishi, for military merit his fief was increased by two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taishi his fief was likewise increased by two hundred households for military merit.

sentences.zh: 為晉平王休祐驃騎中兵參軍，龍驤將軍、南濟陰太守。

translations.literal: He served as Central Army Staff Officer under Prince of Jinping Liu Xiuyou's Rapid Cavalry, General of the Dragon Chariot, and Administrator of Nanjiyin.
translations.idiomatic: He served as central army staff officer under Prince of Jinping Liu Xiuyou's rapid cavalry, as general of the dragon chariot, and as administrator of Nanjiyin.

sentences.zh: 三年北伐，與虜戰，軍敗見殺。

translations.literal: In the third year of the northern campaign he fought the barbarians and was killed when the army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the northern campaign he fought the enemy and was killed when the army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 追贈左軍將軍，太守如故。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the rank of General of the Left Army, his administrator's post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the rank of general of the left army, retaining his administrator's post.

sentences.zh: 李道兒，臨淮人。

translations.literal: Li Dao'er was a native of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dao'er came from Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 本為湘東王師，稍至湘東國學官令。

translations.literal: He originally served as tutor to the Prince of Xiangdong and gradually rose to Director of the National University of the Xiangdong principality.
translations.idiomatic: He originally served as tutor to the Prince of Xiangdong and gradually rose to director of the national university of the Xiangdong principality.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，稍進至員外散騎侍郎，淮陵太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he gradually advanced to Outside the Office Cavalier Attendant and Administrator of Huailing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he gradually advanced to outside-the-office cavalier attendant and administrator of Huailing.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年，兼中書通事舍人，轉給事中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi he also served as Secretariat Gentlemen for Current Affairs and was transferred to Attendant Within the Gates.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taishi he also served as secretariat gentleman for current affairs and was transferred to attendant within the gates.

sentences.zh: 四年，病卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in the fourth year.

sentences.zh: 元徽二年，太尉桂陽王休範奄至新亭，佃夫留守殿內，而道隆領羽林精兵向硃雀門。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui, the Grand Commandant Prince of Guiyang Liu Xiufan suddenly arrived at Xinting; Dianfu remained to hold the palace interior while Daolong led the elite Feathered Forest troops toward the Vermilion Bird Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhui, Grand Commandant Prince of Guiyang Liu Xiufan suddenly arrived at Xinting; Dianfu remained to hold the palace interior while Wang Daolong led elite Feathered Forest troops toward the Vermilion Bird Gate.

sentences.zh: 時賊已至航南，道隆忽召鎮軍將軍劉勔于石頭，勔至，命開航，道隆怒曰：「賊至但當急擊，寧可開航自弱邪！」

translations.literal: At the time the rebels had already reached the south of the floating bridge; Daolong suddenly summoned General Who Garrisons the Army Liu Kan at Stone City; when Kan arrived and ordered the bridge opened, Daolong angrily said: "When rebels arrive one should strike at once—how can one open the bridge and weaken oneself!"
translations.idiomatic: At the time the rebels had already reached the south side of the floating bridge; Daolong suddenly summoned General Who Garrisons the Army Liu Kan at Stone City; when Kan arrived and ordered the bridge opened, Daolong angrily said: "When rebels arrive one should strike at once—how can you open the bridge and weaken our position!"

sentences.zh: 勔不敢複言。

translations.literal: Kan did not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kan did not dare say another word.

sentences.zh: 催勔進戰，勔度航便敗，賊乘勝徑進，道隆棄眾走向台，所乘馬連聳跼不肯前，遂為賊兵及，見殺。

translations.literal: Daolong pressed Kan to advance and fight; Kan judged that once the bridge was crossed they would be defeated; the rebels pressed their victory and advanced straight on; Daolong abandoned the troops and fled toward the palace terrace; the horse he rode repeatedly reared and balked and would not go forward; he was then overtaken by rebel soldiers and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Daolong pressed Kan to advance and fight; Kan judged that crossing the bridge would mean defeat; the rebels pressed their advantage and drove straight forward; Daolong abandoned his troops and fled toward the palace terrace, but the horse he rode repeatedly reared and refused to go forward; rebel soldiers overtook him and killed him.

sentences.zh: 事平，車駕臨哭，贈輔國將軍、益州刺史。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, the imperial carriage came to mourn; he was posthumously granted General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs were settled, the emperor came in person to mourn; he was posthumously granted General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 子法貞嗣。

translations.literal: His son Fazhen inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fazhen inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 楊運長，宣城懷安人。

translations.literal: Yang Yunchang was a man of Huai'an in Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yunchang was a native of Huai'an in Xuancheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 初為宣城郡吏，太守范曄解吏名。

translations.literal: At first he was a clerk of Xuancheng commandery; the Administrator Fan Ye struck his name from the clerical rolls.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was a clerk of Xuancheng commandery; the Administrator Fan Ye struck his name from the clerical rolls.

sentences.zh: 素善射，太宗初為皇子，出運長為射師。

translations.literal: He was skilled at archery; when Emperor Ming was first a prince, Yunchang was sent out as his archery instructor.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at archery; when Emperor Ming was first a prince, Yunchang was sent out as his archery instructor.

sentences.zh: 性謹愨，為太宗所委信。

translations.literal: His nature was cautious and honest; he was entrusted and trusted by Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was cautious and honest; Emperor Ming entrusted and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 及即位，親遇甚厚，與佃夫、道隆、李道兒等並執權要，稍至員外散騎侍郎，南平昌太守。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, intimate treatment was very deep; with Dianfu, Daolong, Li Dao'er, and the rest he jointly held crucial power, gradually reaching Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Administrator of Nanpingchang.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, he was treated with great intimacy; with Dianfu, Daolong, Li Dao'er, and the rest he jointly held crucial power, eventually reaching Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Administrator of Nanpingchang.

sentences.zh: 泰始七年，出侍東宮。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taishi he went out to attend the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taishi he went out to attend the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝即位，與佃夫俱兼通事舍人，加龍驤將軍，轉給事中。

translations.literal: When the Later Deposed Emperor took the throne, he and Dianfu were both made concurrent Communications Attendants, with the additional title General of the Dragon Vanguard, then transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Deposed Emperor took the throne, he and Dianfu were both made concurrent Communications Attendants, with the additional title General of the Dragon Vanguard, then transferred to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以平桂陽王休范功，封南城縣子，食邑八百戶。

translations.literal: For pacifying Prince of Guiyang Liu Xiufan he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Nancheng county with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For pacifying Prince of Guiyang Liu Xiufan he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Nancheng county with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 元徽三年，自安成王車騎中兵參軍，遷後軍將軍，兼舍人如故。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanhui he moved from Staff Major of the Army for Prince of Ancheng's Fast Cavalry to General of the Rear Army, his concurrent Attendant post as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanhui he moved from Staff Major of the Army for Prince of Ancheng's Fast Cavalry to General of the Rear Army, retaining his concurrent Attendant post as before.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：竭忠盡節，仕子恆圖；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Exhausting loyalty and fulfilling integrity is what office-holders constantly aim at;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Exhausting loyalty and fulfilling integrity is what office-holders constantly aim at;

sentences.zh: 隨方致用，明君盛典。

translations.literal: employing men according to their capacities is the splendid canon of enlightened rulers.
translations.idiomatic: employing men according to their capacities is the splendid practice of enlightened rulers.

sentences.zh: 舊非本舊，因新以成舊者也；

translations.literal: What is old was not originally old—it becomes old through the new;
translations.idiomatic: What counts as an old associate was not originally old—intimacy becomes "old" through the new;

sentences.zh: 狎非先狎，因疏以成狎者也。

translations.literal: what is familiar was not familiar at first—it becomes familiar through distance.
translations.idiomatic: what is familiar was not familiar at first—familiarity grows through repeated proximity.

sentences.zh: 而任隔疏情，殊塗一致，權歸近狎，異世同規。

translations.literal: Yet commission separates from distant feeling; different paths reach one end; power returns to the near and familiar; different ages share one rule.
translations.idiomatic: Yet office separates from distant ties; different paths reach one end; power returns to the near and familiar; different ages share one pattern.

sentences.zh: 雖複漢高之簡易，光武之謹厚，猶豐、沛多顯，白水先華，況世祖之泥滯鄙近，太宗之拘攣愛習，欲不紛惑床笫，豈可得哉！

translations.literal: Even though Han Gaozu was simple and easy and Guangwu was cautious and generous, still Feng and Pei produced many who shone forth, and Baishui flowered first—how much more when Emperor Xiaowu was mired and clinging to what was base and near, and Emperor Ming was cramped and bound to beloved habits: to wish that the bedchamber not be thrown into confusion—how could that be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: Even though Han Gaozu was simple and Guangwu cautious and generous, still Feng and Pei produced many who shone forth, and Baishui flowered first—how much more when Emperor Xiaowu was mired in what was base and near, and Emperor Ming cramped by beloved habits: to expect the bedchamber not to fall into confusion—how could that be!
